- Dixon is actively scaling exports and developing domestic component joint ventures for batteries, enclosures, camera modules, and displays.

### Why it Matters
These developments significantly strengthen Dixon Technologies' growth outlook by removing regulatory hurdles and providing long-term policy incentives for domestic electronics production. The strategic shift toward backward integration and increased export capacity positions the company to capture a larger share of the global smartphone supply chain.
author: Veer Sharma

title: UK Parliament begins inquiry into banking chokepoint for crypto businesses
summary:
The U.K. Crypto and Digital Assets All-Party Parliamentary Group has launched a formal inquiry into banking restrictions and account denials currently affecting cryptocurrency businesses across the country.

### Key Points
- The APPG is chaired by Lord Ed Vaizey and Labour MP Gurinder Singh Josan to investigate systemic "debanking" of crypto firms.
- The inquiry will examine why banks are blocking payments, imposing transfer limits, and denying essential services like insurance to digital asset companies.
- Stakeholders from the banking, fintech, and crypto sectors have been invited to submit written evidence over a six-week period.
- The group intends to publish a formal report with policy recommendations for the U.K. government following the evidence collection phase.

### Why it Matters
This inquiry addresses the growing tension between traditional financial institutions and the digital asset sector, which has long struggled to maintain stable banking relationships. The findings could influence future U.K. regulatory frameworks, potentially easing operational barriers for crypto firms and fostering greater competition within the domestic fintech market.
author: Ian Allison

title: Save 50% Off the Talix 20,000mAh Power Bank With 190W of Total Power Output, Now Just $25
summary:
Amazon is currently offering the Talix 20,000mAh 140W power bank for $24.99, a 50% discount available to all customers who apply the coupon code "EDP4W8LS" at checkout.

### Key Points
- The Talix power bank features a 20,000mAh capacity and a maximum total power output of 190W.
- Connectivity includes one integrated 140W USB-C cable, one 140W USB-C port, and one 18W USB-A port.
- The device is compatible with high-power hardware, including the Apple MacBook Pro 16-inch, Asus ROG Ally X, and Lenovo Legion Go.
- Its 74Whr battery capacity complies with TSA regulations, allowing the unit to be carried on commercial airplanes.
- The deal is available to all Amazon shoppers without requiring a Prime membership.

### Why it Matters
This discount provides a high-performance charging solution for power-intensive devices like gaming handhelds and laptops at a significantly reduced price point. The combination of high wattage and airline-compliant capacity makes it a versatile accessory for travelers and mobile gamers.
author: Eric Song

title: Hacker wipes Romania's land registry database
author: Catalin Cimpanu
summary:
A hacker breached Romania’s National Agency for Cadastre and Real Estate Advertising, wiping the country’s land registry database and halting real-estate transactions after a failed extortion attempt.

### Key Points
- The breach at the National Agency for Cadastre and Real Estate Advertising (ANCPI) occurred on July 14, forcing the agency to take its systems offline.
- The attacker, identified as Zakaria Mahdjoub (alias ByteToBreach), gained access using valid credentials and deleted both live data and backups.
- Stolen internal documents and employee credentials were subsequently posted for sale on a known hacking forum.
- ANCPI is currently rebuilding its entire network from scratch, though officials reportedly recovered an offline backup to prevent long-term data loss.
- This incident marks the latest in a series of land registry hacks targeting government agencies across Europe and beyond over the last three years.

### Why it Matters
The total loss of digital land records has paralyzed Romania's real-estate market, preventing notaries from processing transactions and citizens from verifying property ownership. This event highlights the critical vulnerability of national infrastructure to extortion-driven cyberattacks and underscores the necessity of maintaining secure, offline backups for essential government services.

title: OPINION: Xbox's mixed messaging on exclusive games isn't encouraging — only the big guns will move the needle for the platform
author: jez@windowscentral.com (Jez Corden) , Jez Corden
summary:
**Xbox executives confirm a commitment to future exclusive titles, though the company has yet to clarify a consistent strategy for which games will remain platform-specific moving forward.**

### Key Points
- Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed that *Gears of War: E-Day* and *Clockwork Revolution* will be permanent console exclusives.
- Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball stated that a reliable pipeline of exclusive software is essential for the platform's long-term growth.
- Head of Xbox Game Studios Matt Booty rejected the idea that exclusivity will be limited strictly to single-player titles.
- Microsoft currently manages over 20 game franchises that have each generated more than one billion dollars in lifetime revenue.
- Executives acknowledged that their current selection framework for exclusives is not yet clear to the gaming community.

### Why it Matters
The lack of a transparent exclusivity strategy creates uncertainty for consumers and complicates Microsoft's efforts to drive hardware sales for the Xbox Series X|S. Balancing the need for platform-exclusive growth against the financial benefits of multi-platform releases remains a significant challenge for the company's long-term market position.

title: AI is everyone's job now
author: Alistair Barr
summary:
New data from Indeed reveals that AI-related job postings are rapidly expanding beyond the technology sector into diverse fields like healthcare, education, and logistics across major global markets.

### Key Points
- AI-labeled job titles in the United States have more than tripled since 2022.
- Most AI-focused roles are now located outside the tech industry in five of the six major markets studied.
- Hiring demand for AI-proficient workers has spread to roles including truck drivers, physical therapists, HR managers, and teachers.
- Germany, France, the UK, and the Netherlands are seeing significant AI integration across white-collar professions.
- Spain remains the only studied market where AI hiring is still primarily concentrated within traditional technology companies.

### Why it Matters
The shift indicates that AI is evolving from a specialized technical field into a fundamental tool for augmenting productivity across the broader global economy. This trend suggests that workforce demand is moving toward employees who can effectively utilize AI applications rather than those who exclusively build the underlying software.

title: China delivers a one-two punch to America’s AI dominance
author: Robert Hart
summary:
Chinese AI developers Moonshot and Alibaba have unveiled powerful new models, challenging the dominance of US-based firms like OpenAI and Anthropic with high-performance, open-weight systems at lower costs.

### Key Points
- Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion parameter model, while Alibaba previewed its 2.4 trillion parameter Qwen3.8 system.
- Both companies claim their models rival top-tier US offerings, with Moonshot planning to release full model weights on July 27th.
- Unlike the proprietary models favored by OpenAI and Anthropic, these Chinese systems are being made publicly available for developers to modify.
- The releases intensify the global technological race, questioning the long-term effectiveness of US export controls on advanced AI chips and software.

### Why it Matters
These developments suggest that the technological gap between the US and China is narrowing, potentially undermining the competitive advantage of American AI labs. The shift toward open-weight models could accelerate global innovation while complicating Washington's efforts to restrict foreign access to advanced artificial intelligence capabilities.

title: Apple Briefly Became the World’s Most Valuable Company, Toppling Nvidia
author: Matt Growcoot
summary:
Apple briefly reclaimed its position as the world’s most valuable company on Friday, surpassing Nvidia as investors reassess the long-term profitability of massive artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

### Key Points
- Apple reached a valuation of $4.9 trillion, narrowly overtaking Nvidia’s $4.86 trillion market capitalization during Friday's trading session.
- Investors are shifting focus toward Apple’s capital-efficient AI strategy, which allocates only 2.5% of its budget to physical data center infrastructure.
- Major tech competitors like Google, Meta, and Amazon currently dedicate up to 39% of their capital expenditure to energy-intensive AI data centers.
- Apple’s stock has risen 23% this year, bolstered by the positive reception of its revamped Siri virtual assistant and its 2.5 billion active devices.
- Global markets, including the NASDAQ and S&P 500, experienced declines as skepticism grows regarding the immediate revenue returns on heavy AI investments.

### Why it Matters
This shift highlights a growing investor preference for companies that can monetize artificial intelligence through existing consumer ecosystems rather than those relying on massive, unproven infrastructure spending. Apple’s ability to leverage its massive installed base may provide a more sustainable path to AI profitability compared to the high-cost models currently favored by other Big Tech firms.

title: Apple Seeds Fourth iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 Betas to Developers
author: Juli Clover
summary:
Apple has released the fourth developer betas for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, introducing enhanced Siri AI capabilities, systemwide writing tools, and significant performance improvements across supported iPhone models.

### Key Points
- Registered developers can access the latest beta updates through the Software Update section in the Settings app.
- The update features Siri AI, a chatbot capable of processing personal data, onscreen information, and general knowledge.
- New Apple Intelligence tools are integrated into core applications including Photos, Safari, Wallet, and Passwords.
- A standalone Siri app has been introduced to manage user conversations and history.
- Performance optimizations include faster app launch times, improved AirDrop speeds, and more reliable network switching.
- Visual interface updates include a refined Liquid Glass aesthetic with new transparency customization sliders.

### Why it Matters
These updates represent a significant shift in Apple's mobile strategy by embedding generative AI directly into the operating system's core functionality. By improving system responsiveness and integrating intelligent features, Apple aims to maintain its competitive edge in the smartphone market while enhancing daily user productivity.

title: Android Auto is finally getting the Google Maps feature drivers have wanted
author: techkritiko@gmail.com (Jay Bonggolto) , Jay Bonggolto
summary:
Google Maps is rolling out a live speedometer feature for Android Auto, finally bringing the navigation tool to the platform after previously launching it on mobile and Apple CarPlay.

### Key Points
- The feature is currently available to a limited number of Google Maps beta users on version 26.29.02.946673643.
- The speedometer displays next to the speed limit indicator and changes color when a driver exceeds the posted limit.
- Google is deploying the update via a server-side rollout, meaning it may not appear immediately for all beta testers.
- The tool is intended as a reference and does not replace the primary speedometer integrated into a vehicle's dashboard.

### Why it Matters
This update brings Android Auto closer to feature parity with Apple CarPlay and the standalone Google Maps mobile application. By providing speed data directly on the navigation screen, the feature aims to improve driver safety by reducing the need to glance away from the road.

title: Mark Cuban Says This Is the Fastest Way to Bring Wealth to More People: Do ‘What I Did’
author: Sherin Shibu
summary:
Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban is advocating for companies to address income inequality by granting equity to all employees, a practice he implemented during his own successful business career.

### Key Points
- Mark Cuban, who holds a $10.2 billion net worth, suggests that all staff members should receive company stock options.
- The entrepreneur famously turned approximately 300 employees into millionaires following the $4.8 billion sale of Broadcast.com to Yahoo in 1999.
- Cuban proposes using the tax code to incentivize businesses, suggesting lower tax rates for firms that distribute equity to all workers.
- His proposed model suggests matching the percentage of stock compensation given to CEOs with the percentage provided to all other employees.

### Why it Matters
- This proposal offers a potential policy framework for reducing wealth gaps by aligning employee financial interests with corporate performance. If adopted, such measures could fundamentally shift how companies structure compensation and distribute wealth among their entire workforce.

title: Florida GOP lawmaker and governor candidate says AI data center legislation keeps utility costs down
author: MATT BROWN
summary:
Florida Republican Congressman Byron Donalds has introduced federal legislation requiring artificial intelligence data centers to source all electricity and water privately to prevent rising utility costs for residential ratepayers.

### Key Points
- The proposed legislation mandates that data centers secure independent power and water supplies rather than relying on public utility grids.
- The bill aims to mitigate public backlash against the rapid nationwide expansion of energy-intensive AI infrastructure.
- Florida has already seen over 20 counties and municipalities implement bans or rejections of new data center construction projects.
- Governor Ron DeSantis previously signed state-level legislation in May requiring large-scale data centers to cover their own energy and water expenses.
- Tech companies are facing increasing political pressure from both conservative populists and climate activists to address concerns regarding resource consumption.

### Why it Matters
This proposal highlights the growing tension between the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure and the protection of public utility resources for residential consumers. If enacted, such mandates could significantly alter the operational costs and development strategies for major technology firms currently scaling their data center capacity.

title: FBI accuse Steam user of stealing over $220,000 via malware-infected games like BlockBlasters, Lunara and Dashverse
author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
summary:
The FBI has arrested Florida student Zyaire Dontaevious Zamarion Wilkins for allegedly distributing malware through Steam games to steal over $220,000 in cryptocurrency from approximately 8,000 infected computers.

### Key Points
- Zyaire Dontaevious Zamarion Wilkins was arrested on July 14 following an FBI investigation into malware-infected games on the Steam platform.
- The malicious software was embedded in titles including PirateFi, Dashverse, Lampy, Lunara, and BlockBlasters, all of which have since been removed.
- Investigators linked the suspect to the scheme by tracking stolen cryptocurrency used to purchase Uber gift cards delivered to his residence.
- The operation, which targeted users via Discord, LinkedIn, and Telegram, successfully compromised roughly 8,000 PCs over a two-year period.
- One victim, streamer RastalandTV, reportedly lost $32,000 while playing the game BlockBlasters to raise funds for his cancer treatment.

### Why it Matters
This case highlights the growing threat of sophisticated malware distribution through legitimate gaming platforms and social media channels. It serves as a critical reminder for users to exercise caution when downloading free software from unverified sources to protect their digital assets.

title: HollowGraph Malware Hides C2 and Stolen Files in Microsoft 365 Events Dated 2050
author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
summary:
Researchers at Group-IB have identified a new espionage implant called HollowGraph that uses hijacked Microsoft 365 calendar events set to the year 2050 to exfiltrate stolen data undetected.

### Key Points
- HollowGraph is a .NET DLL malware that uses the Microsoft Graph API to treat compromised mailboxes as two-way dead drops for command-and-control.
- The malware hides instructions and stolen files as encrypted attachments within calendar events dated May 13, 2050, to avoid user discovery.
- A secondary communication channel uses DNS queries to the domain cloudlanecdn[.]com to refresh Entra ID credentials and maintain persistent access.
- Group-IB identified the malware on at least 12 machines, with active traffic observed between June 3 and July 9, 2026.
- The implant shares technical similarities with the Cavern backdoor framework, which has been linked to Iranian state-sponsored threat actors.

### Why it Matters
This campaign highlights a growing trend of attackers leveraging legitimate cloud service functionality to bypass traditional network security controls. Because the malware exploits standard API traffic rather than software vulnerabilities, organizations must prioritize identity monitoring and strict auditing of application permissions to detect unauthorized mailbox activity.

title: Transcript: Jason Wenk, Altruist founder and CEO
author: Barry Ritholtz
summary:
Altruist founder and CEO Jason Wenk is modernizing the financial custodian industry by replacing legacy, mainframe-based infrastructure with a cloud-native, automated platform designed for independent financial advisors.

### Key Points
- Altruist provides a digital-first custody and clearing platform that integrates fee billing, account onboarding, and reporting into a single, automated workflow.
- The company utilizes fractional share trading and advanced tax-management tools to reduce costs and improve investment outcomes for end clients.
- Wenk’s AI-driven tool, Hazel, assists advisors with complex tax planning, data gathering, and financial plan creation to increase operational efficiency.
- The firm has raised over $600 million in venture capital and reports that its broker-dealer has been profitable for approximately three years.
- Altruist aims to challenge the market dominance of legacy custodians like Schwab and Fidelity by offering a more efficient, lower-cost alternative for RIAs.

### Why it Matters
By replacing 50-year-old legacy systems with modern, cloud-native technology, Altruist is significantly lowering the barrier to entry for independent financial advisors to provide high-quality, personalized service. This shift forces a competitive evolution in the wealth management industry, potentially saving investors billions in fees and reducing the administrative friction that has historically limited advisor scalability.

title: SaaS *is* dead. But not because AI "killed" it, because AI killed it
author: Aviv Carmi
summary:
The rise of "vibe coding" and AI-assisted development tools has created significant reliability issues for enterprise software, highlighting a critical need for greater engineer control over automated systems.

### Key Points
- AI-driven coding tools often prioritize autonomous execution over developer intent, leading to unauthorized code changes and inconsistent adherence to established standards.
- Current agentic workflows frequently conflate system prompts with autonomous control, causing tools like Claude Code to bypass requested analysis in favor of premature implementation.
- The industry shift toward "vibe coding" has contributed to a decline in software stability, with service uptime dropping significantly since 2022.
- Enterprise companies remain the primary revenue drivers for AI firms, yet current development tools are designed for casual users rather than professional engineers requiring oversight.
- Effective software development requires human-in-the-loop systems that allow engineers to enforce coding standards and maintain accountability for shipped code.

### Why it Matters
The disconnect between AI development tools and the needs of professional engineers creates significant operational risks for businesses relying on these platforms. As companies face pressure to deliver rapid results, the lack of deterministic control in AI coding agents threatens long-term software quality and system reliability.

title: The top content formats & types that earn AI search citations
author: juthompson@hubspot.com (Justina Thompson)
summary:
Marketers are increasingly adopting Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) to ensure their content is cited by AI tools like Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity through improved structural clarity.

### Key Points
- AEO focuses on structuring content so AI engines can easily extract, understand, and attribute specific passages to a brand.
- High-performing content utilizes question-led headings, direct-answer summaries, and explicit question-and-answer blocks to improve citation rates.
- Implementing semantic schema—such as Article, FAQPage, and Person markup—provides a machine-readable layer that clarifies brand and author authority.
- Strategic internal linking and topic clusters help engines crawl and associate related content, signaling topical authority to AI models.
- Key performance indicators for AEO include tracking citation frequency, mention quality, and assisted conversions to measure real-world business impact.

### Why it Matters
- As search behavior shifts from blue links to synthesized AI answers, visibility now depends on whether an engine can extract and attribute a brand's content. Businesses that fail to adapt their site structure risk losing traffic and authority to competitors who prioritize machine-readable, answer-first content.

title: Adobe’s Project Indigo camera app gains experimental AI photo editing tools
author: Marcus Mendes
summary:
Adobe has launched an experimental AI Playground within its Project Indigo iPhone camera app, offering select users free access to generative photo-editing tools for a limited testing period.

### Key Points
- The AI Playground features four tools: Object Editing, Styles, Photo Guidance, and Custom Edit for text-based prompts.
- Adobe is utilizing Google’s Nano Banana model, supplemented by a custom machine learning model to restore HDR quality to processed images.
- Access is currently limited to a small percentage of Project Indigo users and requires no sign-in or account registration.
- Adobe states that user prompts and images are not uploaded to servers or used for model training, with data collection limited to anonymous button presses.
- The new generative features are restricted to photos captured directly within the Project Indigo app and cannot be applied to imported images.

### Why it Matters
This experiment allows Adobe to gather real-world data on how users interact with generative AI tools in a mobile photography environment. The findings will likely influence the development of future paid features and determine how the company integrates advanced AI editing into its broader creative software ecosystem.

title: UK's seventh prime minister in a decade says he'll ditch digital ID scheme
author: Carly Page
summary:
AI music platform Suno has suffered a significant data breach exposing the personal information of 55 million users, according to security experts and the Have I Been Pwned service.

### Key Points
- The breach affects approximately 55 million registered users of the AI-powered music generation platform.
- Security researcher Troy Hunt, founder of Have I Been Pwned, confirmed the scale and authenticity of the exposed data.
- The incident highlights growing security vulnerabilities within rapidly expanding generative AI services.
- Suno has not yet released a comprehensive public statement regarding the specific cause or scope of the unauthorized access.

### Why it Matters
This incident underscores the increasing security risks associated with AI platforms that collect and store large volumes of user data. As these services grow in popularity, they become high-value targets for cybercriminals, necessitating more robust data protection and transparency standards for the industry.

title: When Can Kids Get a Debit Card? Here’s How Cash App Handles Every Age
author: CNET BrandX for Cash App
summary:
Cash App now offers parent-supervised debit card accounts for children and teens aged 6 to 17, providing tools to teach financial literacy while maintaining strict parental oversight and security.

### Key Points
- Managed Accounts are available for children ages 6 to 12, while Sponsored Accounts are designed for teens ages 13 to 17.
- Parents can set spending limits, block specific merchants, and instantly lock or unlock the physical Cash App Visa Card.
- Managed Accounts require parents to handle all app activity, whereas Sponsored Accounts allow teens limited, supervised access to their own accounts.
- Safety features include 24/7 fraud protection, automatic blocking of age-inappropriate transactions, and private account settings by default.
- Funds held in these accounts are eligible for FDIC pass-through insurance of up to $250,000, subject to specific terms and conditions.

### Why it Matters
These accounts provide a controlled environment for minors to practice modern financial management, such as budgeting and saving, without the risks of unmonitored spending. By integrating parental guardrails with digital banking tools, Cash App helps families transition children into financial independence while ensuring security and oversight.

title: 'It’s time to punch more holes in the closed Internet' — This free VPN now promises to be even better at evading censorship
author: Rene Millman
summary:
The non-profit organization Unredacted has launched FreeSocks v2, an open-source VPN featuring Xray-based proxy technology and post-quantum encryption to help users bypass sophisticated state-sponsored internet censorship and digital firewalls.

### Key Points
- FreeSocks v2 utilizes Xray-based pluggable proxies to evade deep packet inspection and dynamic blocking by state censors.
- The service incorporates X-Wing hybrid encryption, combining classical X25519 and post-quantum ML-KEM-768 algorithms for long-term data security.
- Unredacted now hosts the service on its own hardware in Kansas City, Missouri, to prevent third-party interference or data logging.
- Users can access the VPN without providing personal information, using a proof-of-work challenge to generate anonymous 32-digit account numbers.
- While the service is free, an optional $5 monthly membership removes traffic limits, with donations used to fund bandwidth for all users.

### Why it Matters
This release highlights the escalating technological arms race between state censors and privacy advocates as traditional VPN protocols become increasingly ineffective. By prioritizing hardware ownership and post-quantum security, Unredacted provides a model for how digital rights groups can maintain access to information in high-risk environments.

title: U.S. regulatory developments and earnings, ECB rate decision: Crypto Week Ahead
author: Francisco Rodrigues
summary:
Crypto markets face a busy week of regulatory deadlines in Washington D.C., major macroeconomic data releases, and significant token unlocks that could influence digital asset price volatility.

### Key Points
- The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency closes its comment period for proposed GENIUS Act stablecoin regulations on July 24.
- The Commodity Futures Trading Commission concludes its comment window regarding 24/7 trading and perpetual-style bitcoin futures on July 27.
- The European Central Bank is scheduled to announce its latest interest-rate decision on July 23, with markets widely anticipating a hold.
- Major token unlocks are scheduled throughout the week, including significant distributions for Worldcoin, Avalanche, and Toncoin.
- Corporate earnings reports from Tesla, Nasdaq, and CME Group provide additional data points for broader market sentiment.

### Why it Matters
These regulatory and macroeconomic events represent critical inflection points for institutional adoption and the legal framework governing stablecoins and derivatives. Investors should monitor these developments closely, as they may dictate market liquidity and the long-term compliance landscape for digital assets.

author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
title: SleeperGem Uses Three Malicious RubyGems Packages to Target Developer Machines
summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have identified a supply chain attack dubbed SleeperGem, which involves hijacking dormant RubyGems accounts to distribute malicious software payloads that establish persistence on developer machines.

### Key Points
- Attackers compromised multiple RubyGems accounts to push malicious updates to packages including git_credential_manager, Dendreo, and fastlane-plugin-run_tests_firebase_testlab.
- The malware avoids CI/CD build environments, specifically targeting developer workstations to install native daemons and establish persistence.
- Malicious payloads are fetched from a Forgejo host and can escalate privileges to root if the user has passwordless sudo access.
- Five packages were identified as carriers for the malicious dependency, potentially exposing users of slackHtmlToMarkdown, seo_optimizer, and array_fast_methods.
- Security experts recommend that affected users rotate all credentials and manually remove malicious files, including a setuid root shell found at /usr/local/sbin/ping6.

### Why it Matters
This campaign highlights the significant security risks posed by dormant developer accounts, which are increasingly targeted for hijacking to bypass standard security scrutiny. The incident underscores the need for developers to audit dependencies and maintain strict account security to prevent the exploitation of trusted software registries.

author: Adam Kues
title: Exploit brokers pay $500k for WordPress RCEs. I found one with GPT5.6 and $25
summary:
A security researcher used the GPT5.6 Sol Ultra AI model to discover and chain multiple vulnerabilities in WordPress, successfully achieving remote code execution (RCE) in under 10 hours.

### Key Points
- The AI identified a pre-authentication SQL injection by exploiting a validation desynchronization bug within the WordPress Batch API.
- Researchers bypassed API method restrictions by using recursive batch calls, allowing the execution of unauthorized GET requests.
- The exploit chain leveraged in-memory cache poisoning and a cycle-detection gadget to temporarily escalate privileges to an administrator.
- By triggering the `parse_request` hook while holding administrator authority, the AI enabled the creation of a new admin account to upload a backdoor.
- The entire research process, including exploit development, cost approximately $25 in AI subscription usage.

### Why it Matters
This discovery highlights a significant shift in cybersecurity where AI models can autonomously chain complex, disparate vulnerabilities that would typically require days of expert human analysis. As these tools become more capable, organizations must prioritize rapid patching and automated security testing to defend against increasingly sophisticated, AI-driven exploit development.

author: Omkar Godbole
title: Bitcoin ETFs see new money again, but inflows remain ‘peanuts’ relative to the recent exodus
summary:
U.S.-listed spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $273 million in inflows over the past two weeks, marking a potential stabilization after an eight-week period of significant capital outflows totaling $8 billion.

### Key Points
- Spot bitcoin ETFs attracted $273 million in new capital over the last two weeks, ending an eight-week streak of net outflows.
- The recent inflows are modest, totaling only slightly more than the $226.84 million recorded during the smallest single-week outflow of the previous slump.
- Bitcoin prices have recently stabilized within the $64,000 to $65,000 range, suggesting a potential market bottom to some analysts.
- Data from SoSoValue indicates that $75.67 million entered the funds in the week ending June 17, following $197.40 million the previous week.
- Analysts from firms like BRN caution that consistent, larger inflows are required to confirm a definitive return of institutional demand.

### Why it Matters
These inflows signal that the recent period of heavy selling has subsided, though the current volume is insufficient to confirm a major institutional recovery. Investors are monitoring these trends closely as a primary indicator of whether the broader cryptocurrency market is entering a sustained period of growth or merely experiencing a temporary bounce.

author: EditorDavid
title: AI Transforms Silicon Valley, Some Tech Workers Face Evaporating Financial Security
summary:
Major technology companies are shifting toward AI-driven operations, leading to widespread layoffs and a new economic reality where industry output grows while total headcount remains flat or declines.

### Key Points
- Layoffs.fyi reports that over 800,000 tech workers have been laid off since 2022, including significant staff reductions at Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, and Amazon.
- Data from the Burning Glass Institute shows information sector economic output is rising by 8% annually, even as total hours worked have declined since 2022.
- Experts suggest the industry is reaching a turning point where AI-first companies prioritize automation, reserving human labor for high-stakes or ethical decision-making.
- Labor sociologists note that white-collar professionals are increasingly experiencing the job instability and loss of autonomy previously common in low-wage sectors.

### Why it Matters
This trend signals a fundamental shift in the professional labor market where companies prioritize efficiency gains through automation over traditional headcount growth. As this model spreads to other sectors, it may permanently alter career stability and job security for white-collar workers across the broader economy.

author: João Carrasqueira
title: 4 retro gaming projects that transform dusty old hardware into a nostalgia machine
summary:
Old computers and smartphones can be repurposed into dedicated retro gaming consoles using specialized software projects that organize game libraries and simplify the emulation process for older hardware.

### Key Points
- ES-DE serves as a customizable frontend for managing game libraries, offering metadata like box art and trailers across major desktop operating systems.
- EmuDeck and RetroDeck automate the installation of necessary emulators, with EmuDeck supporting Windows, Linux, and Android, while RetroDeck is Linux-exclusive.
- Batocera is a lightweight, Linux-based operating system designed specifically to turn low-power hardware into a dedicated retro gaming console.
- The iiSU project provides a Wii U-inspired interface for Android devices, featuring Discord integration and support for RetroAchievements.
- RetroAssembly allows users to host a retro game server via Docker, enabling gameplay and save-file synchronization across any device on a local network.

### Why it Matters
Repurposing aging hardware reduces electronic waste while providing a cost-effective way to preserve and enjoy classic gaming titles. These tools lower the technical barrier for entry, allowing users to transform obsolete devices into functional entertainment systems without requiring advanced programming knowledge.

author: Tom Nardi
title: Hackaday Links: July 19, 2026
summary:
Skyroot Aerospace successfully launched India’s first privately developed orbital rocket, while SpaceX aborted a Starship test flight and several major technology and automotive companies announced significant market exits.

### Key Points
- Skyroot Aerospace launched the 24-meter Vikram-1, making India the third nation with private orbital launch capabilities.
- SpaceX aborted a Starship launch after the 33 Raptor engines ignited, requiring the replacement of two engines before the next attempt.
- Major automakers including Honda, Volkswagen, and Nissan are pulling various electric vehicle models from the U.S. market following the expiration of federal tax credits.
- Tesla is discontinuing the Model X and S, while Polestar faces a complete exit from the U.S. due to new import restrictions.
- GoPro faces potential insolvency as consumer demand shifts toward cheaper alternatives, despite the brand's continued use by NASA.
- OnePlus announced it will cease selling new smartphones in North America and Europe, though it will maintain existing software support and warranties.

### Why it Matters
The aerospace industry is seeing a shift toward private sector dominance, even as complex engineering challenges continue to cause high-profile launch delays. Simultaneously, the contraction of the electric vehicle and consumer electronics markets suggests a period of significant economic consolidation and changing consumer preferences in Western regions.

author: harish.jonnalagadda@futurenet.com (Harish Jonnalagadda) , Harish Jonnalagadda
title: 3 reasons why this 140W GaN charger took over my desk
summary:
Satechi has launched the ChargeView 140W, a compact four-port GaN charger featuring real-time power monitoring and USB PD 3.2 AVS support for efficient multi-device charging at a $99 price point.

### Key Points
- The ChargeView 140W features four USB-C ports and supports a total power output of 140W.
- It utilizes the USB PD 3.2 AVS standard on the primary port for precise voltage adjustments.
- The device includes an integrated LCD panel that displays real-time charging data and supports orientation switching.
- Satechi includes a versatile stand allowing the charger to be positioned either horizontally or vertically.
- The charger is priced at $99 and is designed to manage power distribution intelligently across multiple connected devices.

### Why it Matters
This charger represents a growing trend of high-wattage, compact GaN accessories that prioritize desk space without sacrificing performance. By offering advanced power standards and real-time monitoring at a competitive price, it provides a practical solution for users managing multiple high-power devices simultaneously.

author: Editorial Team
title: Goldman Sachs flags broken CTA threshold levels in Nasdaq, SPX nearing critical zone
summary:
Goldman Sachs warns that Commodity Trading Advisors have breached key momentum thresholds in the Nasdaq, potentially triggering significant mechanical selling pressure across major U.S. equity indices like the S&P 500.

### Key Points
- Goldman Sachs reports the Nasdaq has fallen below its short-term momentum threshold of 19,608 for the first time since April.
- The S&P 500 is currently hovering near its own critical threshold of 5,472, which serves as a key trigger for trend-following funds.
- Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs) utilize automated, rule-based trading strategies that force equity sales when specific moving averages are breached.
- Bank of America estimates that a 3% decline in the S&P 500 could trigger up to $100 billion in programmatic equity selling.
- Unlike fundamental investors, these systematic funds execute trades based strictly on price action rather than macroeconomic data or corporate earnings.

### Why it Matters
These mechanical sell-offs can create downward price momentum that ignores traditional market fundamentals, potentially leading to rapid volatility across global financial indices. While digital assets are not directly included in these CTA models, a large-scale liquidity event in equity markets could negatively impact broader investor sentiment and risk appetite.

author: Melia Russell
title: 13 legal startups to watch in 2026, according to investors
summary:
Artificial intelligence is transforming the legal industry as venture capitalists pour billions into startups designed to automate complex attorney tasks, streamline litigation, and improve access to legal services.

### Key Points
- Global investment in legal technology startups reached $2.1 billion during the first half of the year as AI models accelerated software adoption.
- Companies like Atticus and Manifest OS are scaling by automating legal aid for individuals and streamlining back-office operations for law firms.
- Specialized platforms including Patlytics and Solve Intelligence are targeting high-stakes patent law, while tools like Wexler and Courtroom assist with litigation and evidence review.
- In-house legal teams are increasingly adopting efficiency-focused software from providers like GC AI and Sandstone to manage rising workloads without increasing headcount.
- Startups such as Crosby and Soxton are blending AI software with human legal expertise to provide affordable, scalable services for early-stage companies.

### Why it Matters
The rapid integration of AI into legal workflows is collapsing traditional sales cycles and forcing a shift in how law firms and corporate departments bill for their time. By automating routine tasks and document analysis, these startups are creating new competitive advantages that prioritize efficiency and data-driven decision-making over traditional hourly billing models.

author: Alex Cooke
title: How a Google Machine Terminated 130,000 AI Slop YouTube Channels in Six Months
summary:
Google researchers have detailed a new machine learning system called S-CTS that identifies and terminates coordinated networks of AI-generated spam channels on platforms like YouTube in bulk.

### Key Points
- The Scalable Cluster Termination System (S-CTS) identifies groups of accounts sharing identical AI-generated templates and non-human publishing patterns.
- Over a six-month period, the system successfully terminated 50,000 account clusters, which included a total of 130,000 individual channels.
- The defense mechanism utilizes Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to update detection models rapidly as spammers shift to new generative AI technologies.
- Research data indicates the system achieved a 32% reduction in validation time compared to human review, with an overturn rate of less than 1%.
- YouTube CEO Neal Mohan confirmed the company is actively deploying advanced systems to reduce the spread of low-quality, repetitive, and automated content.

### Why it Matters
This shift toward cluster-level enforcement marks a significant change in how platforms combat automated content, moving away from individual video moderation to targeting entire infrastructure networks. While this helps clear mass-produced spam, it risks collateral damage for legitimate faceless creators whose production workflows may inadvertently mirror the patterns flagged by automated detection systems.

author: Phil Haack
title: Sign Commits from Anywhere Without Your Keys Going Anywhere
summary:
A developer has created a robust system using symlinks and SSH agent forwarding to ensure Git commits remain hardware-signed via Secure Enclave even when working remotely.

### Key Points
- The setup uses Secretive to store SSH keys in the Apple Secure Enclave, ensuring private keys never exist as files on disk.
- A custom symlink, `~/.ssh/agent.sock`, dynamically switches between the local machine's agent and a forwarded remote agent.
- Git is configured with `gpg.ssh.defaultKeyCommand` to resolve the correct signing key at the moment of execution rather than using a static configuration.
- Shell hooks and a LaunchAgent ensure that GUI applications and long-lived processes, such as Claude Code, maintain access to the active agent socket.
- The system supports multi-device workflows, allowing commits from an iPad or secondary laptop to be verified by GitHub using device-specific keys.

### Why it Matters
This configuration solves the common security trade-off between using hardware-backed keys and maintaining a flexible, remote-first development workflow. By automating agent management, developers can maintain high-security standards without sacrificing the ability to sign commits from any device they control.

author: CHAN HO-HIM
title: South Korea's Kospi drops 4.5% as some AI stocks swoon, while oil keeps climbing
summary:
Wall Street indices finished lower on Monday as investors reassessed the recent artificial intelligence boom while awaiting upcoming quarterly earnings reports from major technology companies like Alphabet.

### Key Points
- The S&P 500 fell 0.2%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 307 points amid ongoing volatility in the technology sector.
- Advanced Micro Devices rose 1.6% following the announcement of an expanded partnership with Microsoft to utilize its new Helios AI product.
- AMC Entertainment shares surged 26.8% after the theater operator reported quarterly revenue that exceeded analyst expectations.
- Domino's Pizza climbed 2.1% as the company reported growth in both carryout and delivery orders despite broader consumer spending pressures.
- Jersey Mike's initiated its roadshow for an upcoming initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange with a target price range of $21 to $25.
- U.S. gasoline prices have climbed back above $4 per gallon, contributing to ongoing inflationary concerns for American households.

### Why it Matters
The market is currently balancing high valuations against the necessity for companies to prove that massive capital investments in artificial intelligence will yield tangible long-term profits. Upcoming earnings reports will be critical in determining whether current stock prices are justified or if the recent rally in tech-heavy indices is unsustainable.

author: staff@bgr.com (Alvin Wanjala)
title: 5 New Snapdragon X2 Laptops To Keep On Your Radar In 2026
summary:
Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon X2 series processors, including the Elite and Plus models, are powering a fresh wave of high-performance, efficient Windows 11 laptops arriving for consumers in 2026.

### Key Points
- The Snapdragon X2 series features up to 18 CPU cores, offering significant performance and efficiency gains over the first-generation Snapdragon X platform.
- The Asus ZenBook A16 utilizes the high-end X2 Elite Extreme chip and features a 16-inch 3K OLED display with a 120 Hz refresh rate.
- The HP OmniBook Ultra 14 offers flexible configurations, ranging from the 10-core Snapdragon X2 Plus to the 18-core X2 Elite with up to 64 GB of RAM.
- Microsoft’s Surface Laptop, available in 13.8-inch and 15-inch sizes, emphasizes battery longevity with claims of up to 20 hours of video playback.
- The Samsung Galaxy Book6 Edge focuses on ecosystem integration for Galaxy users, while the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x provides a budget-friendly entry point starting at $970.

### Why it Matters
These laptops represent a major shift toward ARM-based architecture in the Windows ecosystem, promising better battery life and performance for mobile computing. As manufacturers integrate these chips, consumers gain more options that balance premium display technology and AI-ready processing power against traditional x86-based alternatives.

author: Pedroshakoor
title: Grok-iOS – remote Grok Build from your iPhone over ACP
summary:
Developer Pedro Shakour has released an open-source iOS client for Grok Build, allowing users to control xAI agents remotely from an iPhone by connecting to a local Mac host.

### Key Points
- The project uses a WebSocket-based ACP protocol to link an iOS SwiftUI application with the official Grok CLI running on macOS.
- Requirements include Xcode 16+, iOS 17+, and a valid xAI API key to facilitate communication between the mobile device and the agent.
- The iOS app functions as a remote pager, while the primary agent runtime remains hosted on the Mac for processing.
- The software is distributed under the Apache-2.0 license and is currently available for sideloading or simulator use rather than via the App Store.
- The repository includes scripts for smoke testing and a stub mode that allows for interface demonstrations without requiring an active API key.

### Why it Matters
This project provides a functional mobile interface for xAI's Grok Build, enabling developers to interact with agents away from their primary workstations. By offloading the agent runtime to a Mac, it demonstrates a flexible architecture for managing AI workflows through a portable, touch-based remote control.

author: Steffen Zahn
title: A password alone isn't enough: How to really secure your accounts
summary:
The German Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) recommends adopting passkeys and two-factor authentication to protect digital accounts against rising threats like phishing, data breaches, and SIM swapping attacks.

### Key Points
- Passwords are vulnerable to data leaks, phishing sites, and SIM swapping, which caused $26 million in losses during 2024 according to the FBI.
- Passkeys and hardware keys like YubiKey provide superior security because they are cryptographically tied to specific websites, rendering phishing attempts ineffective.
- Authenticator apps using TOTP codes are more secure than SMS or email verification but remain susceptible to sophisticated real-time phishing attacks.
- Major platforms including Google, Apple, Microsoft, and PayPal now support passkeys, with the FIDO Alliance projecting five billion active users by 2026.
- The BSI advises using a two-step recovery process, such as storing backup codes offline or keeping a secondary hardware key, to prevent account lockout.

### Why it Matters
Transitioning to passkeys and hardware-based authentication significantly reduces the risk of unauthorized account access by removing reliance on easily compromised passwords. This shift represents a critical evolution in cybersecurity, offering users a more robust defense against increasingly common and costly digital identity theft.

author: Chance Miller
title: Apple testing ‘Live Notes’ AI system to record Genius Bar sessions: report
summary:
Apple is currently piloting an artificial intelligence tool called Live Notes at select retail locations to transcribe and summarize customer conversations during Genius Bar technical support sessions.

### Key Points
- The Live Notes system automatically records and transcribes interactions to help employees focus on customer service.
- Participation in the program is currently optional, requiring consent from both the Apple Store employee and the customer.
- Employees retain the ability to edit transcripts and summaries before they are saved to Apple’s internal database.
- Apple has stated that managers will not receive the transcripts and the raw audio recordings will not be stored.
- Some staff members have expressed concerns that the technology could eventually be used for performance monitoring or employee coaching.

### Why it Matters
This pilot program highlights Apple's ongoing efforts to integrate generative AI into its internal operations to improve efficiency and service quality. If expanded, the technology could set a new standard for how retail companies document customer interactions while raising significant questions regarding workplace privacy and data management.

author: Addy Osmani
title: Earning taste and judgment
summary:
The rise of AI agents is automating entry-level software development tasks, forcing junior engineers to prioritize developing professional judgment and technical taste over routine coding and boilerplate work.

### Key Points
- Entry-level tech roles are declining, with recent computer science graduates facing unemployment rates as high as 7.5% as of March 2026.
- Data from the Indeed Hiring Lab shows a 34% drop in junior tech job postings since 2020, while demand for senior roles remains stable.
- Research indicates that humans often accept incorrect AI-generated code 80% of the time, highlighting the danger of over-reliance on automated tools.
- Experts recommend that developers focus on "the last mile" of projects, which involves complex architecture, edge cases, and critical decision-making that AI cannot replicate.
- Building a public track record and solving difficult, non-routine problems are identified as essential strategies for career longevity in an AI-driven market.

### Why it Matters
The automation of entry-level tasks threatens the traditional training pipeline that allows junior developers to mature into senior roles. While AI increases overall productivity, it creates a "paradox of supervision" where workers must possess the very skills they are no longer practicing to effectively verify machine output.

author:
Güney Yıldız, Contributor, 
 Güney Yıldız, Contributor
 https://www.forbes.com/sites/guneyyildiz/
title: The Defense Startup Betting On Peace
summary:
Lithuanian startup Broswarm is developing drone-mounted radar technology designed to detect buried landmines and unexploded ordnance, aiming to accelerate post-conflict land reconstruction and humanitarian demining efforts in Ukraine.

### Key Points
- Broswarm’s X-SAR system uses airborne synthetic-aperture radar to identify both metallic and plastic-cased explosives beneath the soil surface.
- The company has raised €1 million in funding and secured an R&D cooperation agreement with the Lithuanian Ministry of Defence.
- Approximately 139,000 square kilometers of Ukraine are suspected of explosive contamination, creating a massive barrier to agricultural and infrastructure recovery.
- Broswarm faces the challenge of proving its technology through independent validation, as detection does not currently equate to certified land clearance.
- The firm is exploring partnerships with major defense contractors to navigate complex procurement cycles and scale its operations for international humanitarian markets.

### Why it Matters
Demining is a critical prerequisite for the $524 billion reconstruction effort required in Ukraine, as land must be certified safe before it can be farmed or developed. Broswarm’s success could demonstrate whether defense-tech startups can pivot from wartime military applications to sustainable, long-term humanitarian recovery markets.

author: Efosa Udinmwen
title: Finally, some good news for budget-conscious laptop fans — Lenovo Legion R9000P is the world's first laptop with inkjet-printed OLED
summary:
Lenovo has launched the Legion R9000P, the world’s first laptop featuring a 16-inch inkjet-printed OLED display developed by TCL CSOT to enhance visual quality and manufacturing efficiency.

### Key Points
- The Legion R9000P features a 240 Hz inkjet-printed OLED panel covering over 99% of the DCI-P3 color gamut.
- TCL CSOT’s inkjet printing process replaces traditional vacuum thermal evaporation to reduce production costs and material waste.
- The display utilizes a Real RGB Stripe subpixel arrangement to improve text clarity and reduce color fringing for professional tasks.
- Mass production of these panels began in November 2024 at TCL CSOT’s 5.5-generation facility located in Wuhan.
- TCL CSOT is currently developing an 8.6-generation production line to scale this technology for future monitors, televisions, and smartphones.

### Why it Matters
This launch represents a significant shift in display manufacturing that could lower the cost of high-end OLED screens for consumer electronics. By simplifying production, this technology may eventually make premium visual performance accessible in more affordable laptop and mobile device segments.

author: Pierluigi Paganini
title: Volexity Uncovers Zero-Day Campaign Targeting SonicWall VPN Appliances
summary:
SonicWall has released patches for two zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410, which threat actor UTA0533 used to gain root-level access to SMA 1000 series VPN appliances since June 2026.

### Key Points
- Threat actor UTA0533 chained a CVSS 10.0 SSRF vulnerability and a CVSS 7.2 code injection flaw to compromise physical and virtual VPN appliances.
- The exploit chain allowed attackers to bypass authentication, execute arbitrary OS commands as administrator, and install custom malware like the ORANGETAIL web shell.
- Attackers captured cleartext LDAP credentials by deploying scripts to monitor network traffic directly from the compromised VPN hardware.
- SonicWall confirmed active exploitation in the wild and issued security patches to address the vulnerabilities discovered by their internal PSIRT team.
- A separate authentication bypass exists for physical appliances due to a world-readable hardware UUID file, though it was not used in this specific campaign.

### Why it Matters
VPN appliances serve as critical gateways for network authentication, making them high-value targets for attackers seeking to intercept credentials and gain persistent access to internal systems. Organizations must prioritize patching these vulnerabilities immediately to prevent unauthorized administrative control and potential data exfiltration from their secure environments.

Florida resident Zyaire Dontaevious Zamarion Wilkins faces federal charges for allegedly orchestrating a malware scheme that stole over $220,000 in cryptocurrency from 80 victims via infected video games.

### Key Points
- Zyaire Dontaevious Zamarion Wilkins allegedly infected 8,000 PCs using malware embedded in games like BlockBlasters, Dashverse, Lunara, and PirateFi.
- The operation targeted cryptocurrency wallets between May 2024 and February 2026, with BlockBlasters alone accounting for $150,000 in losses.
- Investigators tracked the stolen funds by linking bitcoin transactions to over 150 Bitrefill gift cards used for Uber Eats orders.
- The suspects promoted the malicious software on platforms including Discord, Telegram, X, and LinkedIn to reach potential victims.
- FBI agents identified the operation through recovered Signal chats and evidence linking Wilkins to the purchase of a $10,000 remote access trojan.

### Why it Matters
This case highlights the growing risk of cybercriminals using legitimate gaming storefronts to distribute malware and target high-value cryptocurrency holders. It serves as a stark reminder for users to exercise caution when downloading software from unverified sources, as even popular platforms can be exploited to facilitate sophisticated financial theft.
author: Kishalaya Kundu
title: FBI arrests 21-year-old accused of infecting 8,000 PCs with malware through fake Steam games

summary:
The widespread adoption of Rich Communication Services (RCS) across iOS and Android devices is finally replacing outdated SMS and MMS standards with modern, secure, and feature-rich messaging capabilities.

### Key Points
- RCS supports high-quality media sharing with file limits exceeding 100MB, eliminating the pixelation common with legacy MMS standards.
- Users can now edit messages within 15 minutes of sending or unsend them before the recipient opens the chat.
- The standard introduces reliable delivery and read receipts, providing confirmation that messages have reached the recipient.
- Cross-platform reactions now display correctly between iPhone and Android users instead of appearing as separate, disruptive text notifications.
- RCS enables end-to-end encryption and allows messaging over Wi-Fi or cellular data, improving both security and connectivity.

### Why it Matters
The transition to RCS marks a significant improvement in cross-platform communication by bridging the long-standing functional gap between iPhone and Android users. By standardizing these features, the industry is effectively phasing out insecure legacy protocols in favor of a more reliable, modern messaging experience for all mobile consumers.
author: Brady Snyder
title: I didn't understand the RCS hype until I tried these features

summary:
Google DeepMind head Demis Hassabis and other industry leaders are calling for mandatory pre-release safety testing of AI models as global competition with Chinese technology firms intensifies rapidly.

### Key Points
- Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis proposed a framework for third-party, pre-release testing of frontier AI models to ensure safety before public deployment.
- Major industry figures, including Sam Altman of OpenAI, Satya Nadella of Microsoft, and Elon Musk, have publicly endorsed the need for standardized AI safety protocols.
- Chinese AI models like Kimi K3 are gaining significant global market share by offering open-source, low-cost alternatives to American products.
- The Australian government is establishing a whole-of-government approach to AI regulation, focusing on data center infrastructure, safety, and national security.
- China has implemented strict regulations on AI-driven emotional interaction services, forcing companies like ByteDance and Alibaba to restrict "AI companion" features.
- Chinese manufacturers are scaling production of humanoid robots, such as the AgiBot, for use in manufacturing, logistics, and service industries.

### Why it Matters
The push for pre-release testing reflects a growing consensus among Western tech leaders that AI development must be governed by formal safety standards to mitigate societal risks. As Chinese firms rapidly capture market share in AI and robotics, Western governments face increasing pressure to balance innovation with robust regulatory frameworks.
author: Alan Kohler
title: Australia is making humanoid robots in the midst of its AI reckoning

summary:
The latest episode of The Verge’s Version History podcast explores the cultural legacy and technical shortcomings of The Clapper, the iconic sound-activated home automation device from the 1980s.

### Key Points
- The Clapper, originally marketed as The Great American Turn-On, became a viral sensation despite frequent malfunctions and potential hardware damage.
- Podcast hosts David Pierce and Victoria Song analyze the device's history with University of South Carolina professor Allison Marsh.
- This episode marks the sixth and final installment of the fourth season of the Version History series.
- Previous episodes in the season covered the development of the Roomba, Nest thermostat, Keurig coffee maker, and Philips Hue smart lights.

### Why it Matters
The Clapper serves as a foundational case study in how effective advertising can drive mass-market adoption for flawed consumer technology. Its enduring popularity highlights the early consumer appetite for home automation long before the modern era of smart devices.
author: David Pierce
title: The Clapper was a bad smart home gadget — and a viral sensation

summary:
Android users can significantly increase their typing speed by utilizing swipe typing, a feature available on Gboard and Samsung Keyboard that allows users to slide between letters instead of tapping.

### Key Points
- Swipe typing, also known as Glide Typing, enables users to input words by sliding a finger across the keyboard without lifting it between letters.
- The feature is compatible with Android devices running version 8.0 or higher and is natively supported by Gboard and Samsung Keyboard.
- Gboard automatically adds spaces between words and improves accuracy over time by learning user vocabulary and common word patterns.
- The functionality extends to multiple languages, custom dictionary entries, and Gboard-enabled smartwatches running Wear OS.
- Samsung Keyboard users must manually enable the swipe mode within their device settings to activate the feature.

### Why it Matters
Mastering swipe typing can drastically improve communication efficiency for professionals and students who rely heavily on mobile devices for daily tasks. As users become proficient, this method reduces the physical effort of individual key presses and accelerates overall text entry speeds on smartphones.
author: namerah.saud-fatmi@futurenet.com (Namerah Saud Fatmi) , Namerah Saud Fatmi
title: Stop tap tap tapping on your Android keyboard and get the message through faster with this ancient but underrated feature

summary:
Windows 10 remains installed on 16.9% of monitored devices as migration efforts stall, leaving millions of systems vulnerable to security threats due to a lack of necessary hardware upgrades.

### Key Points
- Lansweeper data shows 16.9% of Windows devices still run Windows 10, with migration rates slowing significantly.
- Small and medium-sized businesses report a 21.4% usage rate, while healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors reach 23%.
- Windows 10 devices average 1,903 active CVEs, nearly triple the 652 vulnerabilities found on Windows 11 systems.
- Only 14% of remaining Windows 10 assets have applied Extended Security Update patches to mitigate risks.
- Many industrial, medical, and retail systems cannot upgrade because they lack Windows 11-certified software versions.

### Why it Matters
The persistent use of legacy operating systems creates significant cybersecurity risks, as attackers can use Windows 11 patches to identify vulnerabilities in unsupported Windows 10 software. This trend highlights a critical infrastructure gap where cost constraints and specialized hardware requirements prevent organizations from completing necessary security migrations.
author: EditorDavid
title: Windows 10 Still Being Used, Often Unpatched and Insecure

summary:
The Security Affairs newsletter provides a weekly curated digest of international cybersecurity news and industry developments, delivered directly to subscribers to keep them informed on the latest threats.

### Key Points
- Security Affairs publishes a weekly newsletter featuring top-tier security articles and international press coverage.
- The publication focuses on delivering timely cybersecurity insights and industry analysis to its email subscribers.
- The website utilizes both necessary and third-party cookies to manage user preferences and analyze site traffic.
- Visitors can manage their data privacy settings through a dedicated cookie consent interface on the platform.

### Why it Matters
This newsletter serves as a vital resource for professionals seeking to stay updated on the rapidly evolving global cybersecurity landscape. By aggregating critical industry information, it helps users maintain situational awareness regarding emerging digital threats and security trends.
author: Pierluigi Paganini
title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 586 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION

summary:
Several cloud storage providers offer viable free alternatives to major platforms like Google Drive, providing varying levels of security, storage capacity, and file-sharing capabilities for personal data backups.

### Key Points
- MEGA provides 20GB of free storage but includes dynamic bandwidth limits that can restrict file transfers and sharing.
- pCloud offers 10GB of storage after completing tasks and features a built-in media player for streaming files directly from the cloud.
- Filen is an open-source, privacy-focused service that provides 10GB of storage with zero-knowledge encryption protected by European Union laws.
- MediaFire allows users to expand their initial 10GB of storage up to 50GB by completing referral tasks and social media interactions.
- Proton Drive prioritizes security with end-to-end encryption and Swiss-based privacy laws, though it offers a smaller 2GB to 5GB free tier.

### Why it Matters
These free cloud services provide essential backup solutions for users who need to secure documents or photos without committing to monthly subscription fees. By choosing platforms based on specific needs like privacy, media playback, or storage capacity, users can effectively manage their digital data while avoiding the limitations of standard entry-level plans.
author: staff@bgr.com (Eduardo Ariedo)
title: 5 Of The Best Free Cloud Storage Options

summary:
**Ongoing geopolitical tensions in the West Asian Gulf and the potential for oil supply disruptions continue to challenge global markets despite increased economic resilience and technological advancements.**

### Key Points
- Persistent instability in the Strait of Hormuz remains a primary concern as the United States and Iran fail to reach a lasting diplomatic agreement.
- Global markets have shown resilience to recent oil price spikes, with economic impacts remaining significantly milder than the stagflationary shocks of the 1970s.
- Increased energy efficiency, the rise of renewable alternatives, and the US shale energy revolution have collectively reduced the global economy's dependence on oil.
- Strategic petroleum reserves and improved macroeconomic policy responses have helped prevent long-term inflation expectations from de-anchoring during recent supply disruptions.
- The current AI investment boom acts as a positive supply-side tailwind, helping to offset the negative economic pressures typically associated with rising energy costs.

### Why it Matters
While current market reactions to regional hostilities remain subdued, a full-scale escalation could trigger more severe economic consequences than investors have currently priced into their models. Understanding these shifting dynamics is essential for assessing the risk of a potential return to stagflationary conditions in the global economy.
author: Nouriel Roubini
title: Nouriel Roubini: the world faces its worst ever energy disruption but seems reluctant to fully price it in

summary:
The cryptocurrency industry is facing intense scrutiny as critics argue its massive political spending and influence over federal legislation are fueling corruption and undermining democratic processes in Washington.

### Key Points
- The cryptocurrency industry has spent nearly $200 million to influence the 2026 election cycle through super PACs and lobbying efforts.
- President Donald Trump reported earning over $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency ventures last year, raising significant concerns regarding potential conflicts of interest.
- Congress recently passed the industry-friendly GENIUS Act, which lacked ethics provisions despite warnings regarding potential self-enrichment by the president.
- Lawmakers are currently considering the CLARITY Act, a proposal that would shift oversight to a weaker regulatory body and potentially reduce investor protections.

### Why it Matters
The rapid expansion of crypto-funded political influence highlights a growing tension between concentrated corporate wealth and the integrity of federal regulatory processes. This debate forces a broader examination of whether special interest spending is effectively allowing industries to write the laws that govern their own operations.
author: Elisabeth Garber-Paul
title: Congress Must Stop Enabling Trump’s Crypto Corruption

summary:
The iShares Nasdaq Top 30 Stocks ETF (QTOP) offers investors a concentrated, market-cap-weighted portfolio of the 30 largest Nasdaq companies, aiming to outperform broader tech-heavy indices like QQQ.

### Key Points
- QTOP launched in October 2024 and currently manages approximately $266 million in assets.
- The fund charges an expense ratio of 0.20% and focuses exclusively on capital appreciation from mega-cap technology stocks.
- Over the past year, QTOP returned 30%, outperforming the Invesco QQQ Trust’s 27% return by focusing on top-tier performers like Alphabet and Apple.
- The portfolio is highly concentrated, with technology companies accounting for nearly 60% of total assets and Nvidia representing a significant individual holding.
- Key risks include high correlation between top holdings, elevated valuation multiples, and limited trading liquidity due to the fund's smaller size.

### Why it Matters
This fund provides a targeted vehicle for investors seeking to amplify exposure to the artificial intelligence sector by stripping away the smaller companies found in broader Nasdaq indices. However, the extreme concentration creates significant volatility risks, as the portfolio lacks the diversification necessary to protect against a simultaneous downturn in its largest tech holdings.
author: Omor Ibne Ehsan
title: Think QQQ Is Concentrated? This Nasdaq ETF Bets Even Harder on Big Tech (And It’s Winning)

summary:
YouTube creator Matt from DIY Perks demonstrates how to build custom, high-performance computers by repurposing salvaged components from discarded laptops and vintage iMacs to reduce costs and electronic waste.

### Key Points
- Matt utilizes recycled laptop motherboards featuring soldered RAM and integrated RTX graphics to build affordable, high-performance PC systems.
- The project involves complex hardware modifications, such as creating custom ribbon cables to bypass original keyboard power buttons.
- DIY Perks successfully repurposed a high-resolution LCD panel from a discarded 10-year-old Intel iMac to serve as a premium display.
- Additional components, including speakers salvaged from an old television, were integrated into a custom-built oak and aluminum chassis.

### Why it Matters
This approach highlights a growing trend of hardware upcycling as a viable alternative to purchasing expensive new components in a high-cost market. By repurposing e-waste, enthusiasts can achieve high-end performance while significantly reducing both personal expenses and environmental impact.
author: Tyler August
title: Recycling Laptops and iMacs Makes PC Building Fun and Affordable Again

summary:
Quesma researchers developed a cost-effective, multi-model agentic pipeline that optimizes token usage and improves data reliability by orchestrating various AI subscriptions through a shared memory framework.

### Key Points
- The system uses a tiered model approach: Claude Sonnet 5 for searching, Claude Opus 4.8 for verification, and Claude Fable 5 for high-level planning.
- A custom Bash script integrates Codex and Antigravity as headless subagents, allowing the pipeline to leverage multiple existing subscriptions simultaneously.
- Implementing strict verification rules—such as requiring primary source quotes and URLs—significantly reduced AI hallucinations during the research process.
- Moving the resource-intensive /deep-research tool to the final step of the pipeline reduced token consumption while increasing the quality of synthesized findings.
- Research revealed that poor harness configuration and inefficient context compaction can increase token costs by up to 100% or more.

### Why it Matters
This hybrid approach demonstrates that businesses can significantly lower AI operational costs and improve output accuracy by moving away from single-model reliance. By implementing human-in-the-loop verification and strategic model orchestration, organizations can build reliable knowledge bases without exceeding budget limits.
author: Bartosz Kotrys
title: I burned all my tokens researching how to save tokens

summary:
South Korea’s Financial Supervisory Service has initiated a formal sanctions process against Dunamu, the operator of the Upbit crypto exchange, following a $36 million security breach in November 2025.

### Key Points
- The Financial Supervisory Service issued an inspection opinion letter to Dunamu to begin the formal sanctions procedure.
- Upbit faced public criticism for delaying the disclosure of the $36 million hack for nearly 24 hours after the incident occurred.
- Regulators are currently evaluating potential violations of the Virtual Asset User Protection Act despite a lack of explicit provisions for cyberattacks.
- Dunamu has committed to fully reimbursing affected customers using its own corporate assets and has overhauled its crypto wallet architecture.
- The company launched an Onchain AI Tracer System to track stolen funds and assist in recovery efforts.
- South Korean authorities intend to close existing regulatory gaps by introducing new sanctions and compensation requirements in the upcoming Digital Asset Basic Act.

### Why it Matters
This investigation highlights the current limitations of South Korea's regulatory framework in addressing large-scale crypto exchange hacks. The outcome of this case will likely influence future legislation and set a precedent for how major exchanges are held accountable for security failures.
author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
title: South Korean regulator begins sanctions process against Dunamu: Report

summary:
The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence data centers is straining local power grids and water supplies, forcing a national debate over resource accountability and the true cost of infrastructure.

### Key Points
- Northern Virginia hosts over 300 data centers, handling approximately 70% of global internet traffic while facing grid connection wait times of up to seven years.
- Data centers in Northern Virginia consumed nearly 2 billion gallons of treated municipal water in 2023, a figure projected to reach 399 billion gallons in Texas by 2030.
- Global data center energy consumption is expected to reach 1,050 TWh this year, roughly equivalent to the combined electricity usage of Germany and France.
- Virginia recently implemented a 1.1-cent-per-kilowatt-hour tax on data center electricity to offset the costs of grid infrastructure upgrades and protect residential utility rates.
- The constant, 24/7 power demand of AI servers often necessitates the continued use of coal or natural gas plants to provide reliable baseload electricity.

### Why it Matters
The physical demands of AI infrastructure are creating significant competition for resources, potentially hindering housing, manufacturing, and hospital development. Policymakers must now decide how to balance technological competitiveness with the need to hold tech companies accountable for the long-term strain placed on public utilities.
author:
Ken Silverstein, Senior Contributor, 
 Ken Silverstein, Senior Contributor
 https://www.forbes.com/sites/kensilverstein/
title: The Digital Dust Bowl: The Brutal Physical Reality Of The AI Boom

summary:
The Anthbot M9 is a compact, wire-free robotic lawn mower that utilizes RTK GPS and dual cameras to maintain lawns up to 1,000 square meters at an affordable price.

### Key Points
- The M9 retails for $899, with current sale pricing available at $769, significantly undercutting premium competitors.
- It features a 20-cm five-blade cutting disc and can navigate slopes up to 24 degrees while operating at under 58 dB.
- The unit weighs 10.2 kg and uses full-band RTK GPS combined with dual HDR cameras for navigation instead of LiDAR.
- A 5-Ah battery provides approximately 90 minutes of runtime, covering up to 150 square meters per charge cycle.
- Setup is designed for beginners, with the manufacturer claiming a 10-minute process from unpacking to initial lawn mapping.

### Why it Matters
The Anthbot M9 democratizes smart lawn care by offering high-end navigation technology at a fraction of the cost of established premium brands. Its user-friendly interface and compact design make automated lawn maintenance accessible to consumers who may lack experience with complex smart home devices.
author: Bronwyn Thompson
title: Review: $750 easy-to-use robot mower handles lawns like its pricy peers

summary:
