The transition away from crypto-backed funding reflects a broader stabilization effort within the esports sector as organizations prioritize reliable revenue streams over speculative partnerships. This shift signals a maturing market that is increasingly cautious about financial sustainability following the widespread collapse of digital asset sponsors.

author: John T. Haller
title: VeraCrypt Portable 1.26.29 (free disk encryption) Released
summary:
The latest version of VeraCrypt Portable has been released, offering users a free, open-source disk encryption utility that integrates seamlessly with the PortableApps.com platform for secure data management.

### Key Points
- VeraCrypt Portable provides full disk encryption and virtual volume creation based on the original TrueCrypt 7.1a software.
- The utility supports multiple encryption algorithms, including AES, Serpent, and TwoFish, alongside security tokens and keyfiles.
- The software is packaged in the PortableApps.com format, allowing for automatic installation, settings preservation, and platform integration.
- Users can update the application directly through the PortableApps.com platform or by downloading the installer from the official project homepage.

### Why it Matters
This update ensures that users can maintain robust data security across various devices without requiring a permanent installation on a host computer. By streamlining the encryption process for portable drives, the tool provides a critical privacy solution for individuals who need to protect sensitive information while working on the go.

title: 5 Disadvantages Of Buying A Used Laptop
summary:
Purchasing a used laptop can offer significant cost savings, but buyers must navigate risks including hidden hardware damage, degraded battery life, limited warranty coverage, and potential software compatibility issues.

### Key Points
- Used laptops often feature older processors that may struggle with modern resource-intensive software or lack compatibility with newer operating systems like Windows 11.
- Internal components such as batteries and storage drives have finite lifespans, and previous usage often results in reduced performance or imminent hardware failure.
- Pre-existing damage, such as faulty ports, failing fans, or screen defects, may not be immediately apparent during a casual inspection.
- Private sellers rarely provide warranties, leaving buyers financially responsible for expensive repairs like motherboard replacements.
- Tools like "powercfg /batteryreport" for batteries and CrystalDiskInfo for storage drives can help assess the health of critical components before finalizing a purchase.

### Why it Matters
Understanding these risks is essential for consumers to avoid unexpected repair costs that can quickly negate the initial savings of a secondhand purchase. Evaluating the trade-offs between price and long-term reliability helps ensure that a used device remains a practical investment rather than a financial burden.
author: staff@bgr.com (Kazim Alvi)

title: Get Office 2021 + Windows 11 Pro lifetime access for just $39.19 today only
summary:
StackCommerce has released a comprehensive series of 2026 consumer technology buying guides covering essential hardware, home robotics, cybersecurity software, and networking solutions for modern home and office environments.

### Key Points
- The collection features specialized guides for Dell and Alienware laptops, monitors, and gaming gear.
- Home maintenance technology is covered through dedicated buying guides for ECOVACS robot vacuums and Navimow robotic lawn mowers.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy resources include guides for 1Password, Avast, Norton, and Optery.
- Networking and performance hardware are addressed via TP-Link mesh Wi-Fi, MSI Wi-Fi 7, and Seagate external storage guides.
- Gaming-focused content includes recommendations for GIGABYTE AI laptops, ROG custom keyboards, and ZOTAC graphics cards.

### Why it Matters
These guides provide consumers with curated purchasing advice across a wide range of competitive technology sectors as manufacturers transition toward AI-integrated hardware and advanced connectivity standards. By consolidating expert recommendations, the series helps users navigate complex product ecosystems to make informed decisions for their home and professional setups.
author: DealPost Team

title: The debate over what's making it harder for college grads to get hired
summary:
UK fintech firm Revolut will mandate three days of weekly in-office attendance for interns and recent graduates by 2027 to improve mentorship and professional development for early-career employees.

### Key Points
- Revolut plans to increase its intake of interns and graduate program participants to 500 in 2027, up from 300 this year.
- Research from the New York Federal Reserve indicates that remote work environments significantly reduce the amount of constructive feedback provided to junior staff.
- A study by Peter John Lambert and Yannick Schindler suggests remote work has contributed to a 29% decline in entry-level hiring across several countries.
- University of Pittsburgh professor Mark Ma found that companies prioritizing AI integration are increasingly eliminating junior-level roles that can be automated.
- A 2025 Gallup survey shows only 25% of Gen Z workers prefer full-time remote work, favoring hybrid models for better mentorship.

### Why it Matters
The shift toward mandatory in-office requirements for junior staff highlights a growing tension between flexible work preferences and the need for professional development. As companies weigh the impacts of remote work and AI, the declining availability of entry-level positions poses a significant challenge for new graduates entering the labor market.
author: Tim Paradis

title: Is the Oura membership worth it? 5 reasons why I think it is
summary:
The newly released Oura Ring 5 features a refined design, but users must pay a $5.99 monthly subscription fee to access the full suite of health and wellness insights.

### Key Points
- The Oura Membership is optional, but non-subscribers are limited to only three basic metrics: readiness, sleep, and activity scores.
- Paid features include 24/7 heart rate tracking, blood oxygen sensing, advanced sleep analysis, and AI-powered health coaching.
- The Oura app supports third-party integrations with platforms like Strava, Health Connect, and Withings scales.
- Automatic activity detection tracks diverse movements, including workouts, walking, and daily tasks like yard work.
- Oura Membership costs can be covered using Flexible Spending Account (FSA) or Health Savings Account (HSA) funds.

### Why it Matters
The subscription model allows Oura to continuously fund research and software updates, distinguishing its product lifecycle from competitors that offer hardware without ongoing feature development. For users, this creates a trade-off between a higher long-term cost of ownership and access to a more comprehensive, evolving health-tracking ecosystem.
author: derrek.lee@futurenet.com (Derrek Lee) , Derrek Lee

title: I switched to OLED for my entire setup, but I had to keep an LCD around just for coding
summary:
QD-OLED and W-OLED monitors currently struggle with text clarity for productivity tasks due to non-standard subpixel arrangements that conflict with Windows and macOS font rendering software like ClearType.

### Key Points
- QD-OLED panels use a triangular subpixel layout, while W-OLED adds a white subpixel, both of which cause color fringing on text.
- Windows ClearType and macOS text renderers are optimized for traditional RGB-stripe subpixel arrangements found in standard IPS panels.
- Automatic Brightness Limiter (ABL) technology in OLED displays causes inconsistent brightness levels when viewing large white windows like code editors.
- Upcoming 2026 display panels from Samsung and LG aim to resolve these issues by adopting V-Stripe and RGB-stripe layouts.
- High pixel density, such as 4K resolution on smaller screens, can mitigate fringing, but current ultrawide options often lack sufficient density for sharp text.

### Why it Matters
The incompatibility between OLED subpixel structures and operating system font rendering creates significant visual fatigue for professionals who spend hours reading text. While OLED remains superior for gaming, the current hardware limitations make traditional IPS panels a more reliable and consistent choice for coding and document-heavy workflows.
author: Joe Rice-Jones

title: iPhone 17 Pro Max buried in America’s 250th anniversary time capsule: to be opened in 2276
summary:
A time capsule containing an iPhone 17 Pro Max in Cosmic Orange has been buried to commemorate America’s 250th anniversary, with plans to unseal the device in 2276.

### Key Points
- The time capsule includes representative items from every U.S. state to document the current era.
- The iPhone 17 Pro Max is stored with digital artifacts saved within the device's Notes application.
- Experts suggest the phone's battery will likely degrade long before the scheduled 250-year storage period concludes.
- The capsule is officially designated to remain sealed until America’s 500th anniversary in the year 2276.

### Why it Matters
This project highlights the challenges of digital preservation as physical hardware and battery technology struggle to survive over multi-century timelines. It serves as a cultural experiment regarding how future generations will access and interpret the personal technology defining our current digital age.
author: Michael Burkhardt

title: Week in review: SimpleHelp vulnerability exploited, Oracle EBS Payments flaw under attack
summary:
Recent cybersecurity reports highlight active exploitation of SimpleHelp and Oracle E-Business Suite vulnerabilities, alongside growing security concerns regarding the rapid integration of AI features into enterprise software products.

### Key Points
- Attackers are actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-48558) in SimpleHelp RMM to deploy the Djinn Stealer malware.
- A critical flaw in the Oracle E-Business Suite Payments module (CVE-2026-46817) is currently under active exploitation by threat actors.
- Researchers identified six vulnerabilities affecting AirDrop and Quick Share protocols, impacting approximately five billion devices across major mobile and desktop operating systems.
- Mozilla’s 0DIN team warned that AI-powered coding agents are susceptible to indirect prompt injection attacks via malicious GitHub repositories.
- A suspected member of the Scattered Spider hacking group was extradited to the U.S. for an $8 million cryptocurrency ransom scheme.

### Why it Matters
The surge in vulnerabilities linked to AI-integrated tools and widely used file-sharing protocols demonstrates that rapid feature deployment is outpacing current security testing capabilities. Organizations must prioritize patching known exploits and re-evaluating their risk models to prevent attackers from leveraging these increasingly common entry points.
author: Help Net Security

title: This underrated Android feature gave me the work-life boundary I couldn't get any other way
summary:
Android users can improve digital well-being and productivity by utilizing built-in user profiles and Work Profiles to separate personal, professional, and distraction-free environments on a single device.

### Key Points
- Android user profiles allow owners to create distinct, isolated environments with separate home screens, app sets, and notification settings.
- The Work Profile feature, managed via mobile device management (MDM) systems, enables users to pause work-related apps and notifications outside of business hours.
- Guest mode provides a temporary, secure profile for sharing a device without exposing personal data, photos, or private accounts.
- Users can manage these settings by searching for "Multiple users" in the Android system settings or via the Quick Settings panel.
- While widely available on stock Android, some manufacturers, such as Samsung, may limit standard user profile features in favor of enterprise-managed Work Profiles.

### Why it Matters
Leveraging these built-in tools helps users establish clear digital boundaries, reducing the stress of constant work notifications and minimizing distractions during personal time. This functionality effectively eliminates the need for carrying a second handset to maintain a healthy work-life balance.
author: Anu Joy

title: What Sky buying ITV could mean for your favourite shows
summary:
Sky, owned by Comcast, has announced a £1.6bn deal to acquire ITV’s television and streaming business, aiming to create a powerful commercial competitor to global streaming giants in Britain.

### Key Points
- Sky will acquire ITV’s broadcast channels and streaming platform, ITVX, while ITV Studios will remain a separate entity owned by current shareholders.
- ITV is legally required to maintain free-to-air public service broadcasting until at least 2034, ensuring current shows remain accessible without a paywall.
- The deal includes a supply agreement ensuring ITV Studios continues producing content for the network, including popular shows like Coronation Street and Love Island.
- Sky intends to leverage ITV’s massive audience reach and public service prominence to bolster its own streaming and sports broadcasting capabilities.
- ITN’s contract to produce ITV news remains in effect until 2031, though the long-term future of the partnership remains subject to future corporate strategy.

### Why it Matters
This acquisition represents a significant consolidation of the British media landscape, positioning a US-owned entity as a dominant force in both free-to-air and subscription television. By integrating ITV’s reach with Sky’s technical infrastructure, the deal aims to create a formidable rival to international streamers like Netflix and Disney Plus.
author: https://www.facebook.com/bbcnews

title: Amentum Holdings (AMTM) Appears Attractive With New Contract Awards
summary:
Amentum Holdings Inc. has secured a five-year contract from the General Services Administration to provide AI-driven supply chain management services for U.S. military operations across the Indo-Pacific region.

### Key Points
- The General Services Administration awarded Amentum a 60-month firm-fixed price contract on June 17.
- Amentum will manage supply chain logistics for the Pentagon and federal agencies operating in Japan.
- The program utilizes AI-integrated techniques to enhance predictive analysis, demand forecasting, and catalog management.
- Services are designed to support military operational readiness within the United States Indo-Pacific Command area of responsibility.
- Amentum provides specialized engineering, cybersecurity, and logistics solutions for government and defense clients.

### Why it Matters
This contract reinforces Amentum’s role as a critical logistics partner for the U.S. military in a strategically sensitive geopolitical region. By integrating AI into supply chain operations, the company aims to improve efficiency and delivery reliability for federal installations operating in challenging environments.
author: Muhammad Ali Khalid

title: iPhone 18 Pro Leaks Reveal Apple’s Move to an Ultra-Efficient 2Nm Chip
summary:
A massive data breach at Apple supplier Tata Electronics has exposed over 630GB of confidential schematics and technical specifications regarding the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro flagship smartphone.

### Key Points
- Hackers infiltrated Tata Electronics systems, leaking proprietary documents including A20 Pro chip architecture and device design schematics.
- The A20 Pro chip features a 96-bit memory bus and relocated RAM to improve thermal management and multitasking performance.
- New hardware includes a 24MP front-facing camera, under-display Face ID 2.0, and a larger vapor chamber cooling system.
- The device introduces "Ganymede" C2 modem technology, enabling 5G connectivity via satellite for improved remote communication.
- Aesthetic updates include a seamless back glass design and a new cherry red color option.

### Why it Matters
This breach highlights critical vulnerabilities within Apple’s global supply chain and the significant risks associated with protecting intellectual property at third-party manufacturing partners. The incident will likely force Apple to implement stricter cybersecurity protocols and encryption standards to prevent future leaks of sensitive product development data.
author: Roland Hutchinson

title: Windows Central Podcast: The path ahead for Xbox with Jez Corden
summary:
The Windows Central Podcast examines the current state of Xbox under CEO Asha Sharma, addressing studio closure rumors, rising hardware costs, and the future of next-generation console strategy.

### Key Points
- New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is navigating corporate belt-tightening driven by massive Microsoft-wide investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure.
- Rising component costs, specifically RAM, have rendered the traditional console subsidy model unsustainable for both Microsoft and Sony.
- Microsoft is evaluating the future of first-party studios, including potential sales or closures of teams like Ninja Theory and Undead Labs.
- The upcoming "Helix" console project faces internal debates regarding whether to function as an open Windows-based device or a closed ecosystem.
- New technology codenamed "Positron" may allow users to convert physical disc ownership into permanent digital licenses on their Microsoft accounts.

### Why it Matters
These shifts signal a fundamental change in the gaming industry as hardware manufacturers struggle to balance premium pricing with the declining profitability of traditional consoles. The potential move toward an open Windows ecosystem or all-digital models reflects a broader effort to adapt to the dominance of free-to-play titles and rising development costs.
author: zac.bowden@futurenet.com (Zac Bowden) , Zac Bowden

title: The EZVIZ EP4 is a great home security camera for renters — but its facial recognition won't stop it from spamming you with alerts when you come home
summary:
The EZVIZ EP4 Wire-Free Peephole Door Viewer offers a subscription-free, easy-to-install security solution for renters, though it currently suffers from persistent, unavoidable facial recognition notification issues.

### Key Points
- The device installs in approximately 10 minutes by replacing an existing door peephole without requiring drilling or permanent modifications.
- It features 4K video recording and supports local storage via a microSD card up to 512GB, eliminating the need for mandatory cloud subscriptions.
- The camera includes AI-powered person identification, though users cannot currently disable alerts for recognized faces, including their own.
- The unit is priced at £229.99 in the UK, with battery life lasting up to 120 days depending on usage frequency.
- The field of view is optimized for identifying visitors but does not capture packages left directly on the doorstep.

### Why it Matters
This device provides a practical, non-destructive security alternative for apartment dwellers and renters who are typically restricted from installing traditional wired doorbells. While the hardware design is highly accessible, the current limitations in notification settings may frustrate users seeking a more refined, automated smart home experience.
author: catherine.ellis@futurenet.com (Cat Ellis) , Cat Ellis

title: Deals: Galaxy S26 and S26 Ultra prices drop further, Xiaomi 17T and 17T Pro get first price cuts
summary:
Retailers are offering significant post-Prime Day discounts on various smartphones, including the Samsung Galaxy S26 series, Xiaomi 17T models, and Motorola Razr 70 devices, following recent market shifts.

### Key Points
- The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 12/512GB model is currently discounted by €60, while the S26 12/256GB variant is €50 cheaper than two weeks ago.
- Xiaomi 17T and 17T Pro models have transitioned from launch promotions involving free tablets to direct price reductions.
- The Nothing Phone (1) has reached its end-of-life status after receiving its final security update, prompting potential upgrades to the Android 15-based Nothing Phone (3).
- Motorola Razr 70 and 70+ models are on sale, featuring 6.9-inch LTPO displays and distinct hardware specifications like the Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 chipset in the plus model.

### Why it Matters
These price adjustments provide consumers with opportunities to purchase premium mobile hardware at lower costs following major retail events. Tracking these fluctuations helps buyers navigate the product lifecycles of major manufacturers like Samsung, Xiaomi, and Motorola.
author: Peter

title: Tasmania moves to ban 'disgraceful' non-consensual sharing of sexual imagery
summary:
The Tasmanian government has announced plans to criminalize the non-consensual sharing of intimate images, including revenge porn and AI-generated deepfakes, to address rising rates of image-based sexual abuse.

### Key Points
- Tasmania is the final Australian jurisdiction to introduce legislation specifically targeting non-consensual image sharing.
- The proposed laws cover various forms of abuse, including revenge porn and AI-generated deepfakes.
- Draft legislation is scheduled for public consultation by the end of this year.
- The reforms follow a high-profile incident involving deepfake images of 21 schoolgirls shared in a group chat.
- Advocates, including Engender Equality, are calling for tech companies to take greater responsibility for illegal content on their platforms.

### Why it Matters
These reforms aim to close legal loopholes that have previously left victims without clear pathways to justice or police support. By establishing criminal consequences, the state intends to deter perpetrators and provide better protection for victims of digital sexual violence.
author: Crystal McKay

title: Alibaba Bans Claude Code: The Backdoor Scare Explained
summary:
Alibaba has banned the use of Anthropic’s Claude Code across its engineering divisions following reports that the tool contained covert anti-distillation logic targeting specific geographic IP ranges.

### Key Points
- Reports indicate Claude Code used hidden system prompts and IP filtering to detect and disrupt potential model extraction attempts.
- Alibaba’s security team flagged the tool for unauthorized data transmission and opaque behavior that prevented internal auditing.
- Anthropic reportedly acknowledged the feature as an intellectual property protection measure and pledged to remove it in a future update.
- The incident originated from community-led reverse engineering, which identified anomalous network traffic and hidden instructions within the software.
- Other technology firms are reportedly reviewing their AI tool deployments, though no further public bans have been confirmed.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights a growing tension between AI developers protecting proprietary models and the enterprise need for transparent, auditable software. It underscores the necessity for organizations to rigorously vet AI coding assistants, as covert features can create significant security and compliance risks for sensitive corporate environments.
author: Matt Mickiewicz

title: Spain Blacklists Palantir Over Domestic Security Concerns
summary:
Spain has blacklisted U.S. data analytics firm Palantir from government contracts following security evaluations by the National Intelligence Center and the Ministry of Defense regarding sensitive data handling.

### Key Points
- Spain’s National Intelligence Center and Ministry of Defense cited concerns over potential foreign interference and unauthorized access to sensitive data.
- Palantir has provided surveillance and predictive policing software to Spanish law enforcement and border control agencies since 2017.
- The blacklisted contracts were valued at approximately €10 million, according to procurement documents reviewed by Reuters.
- Officials expressed specific concerns regarding compliance with Spanish data protection laws and the U.S. Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.
- A Palantir spokesperson disputed the allegations, claiming the company’s technology is secure and that they have not received formal notification of the ban.

### Why it Matters
This decision reflects growing European skepticism toward U.S. tech dominance and signals a stricter approach to data sovereignty within the European Union. The move could set a precedent for other member states to increase scrutiny of foreign technology providers, potentially impacting Palantir's future expansion across the continent.
author: Chase Codewell

title: AI XRP Price Prediction: Claude Fable 5 Predicts the XRP Price for End of 2026
summary:
XRP is currently trading near $1.15 following a volatile first half of 2026, with the AI model Claude Fable 5 projecting a year-end base price target of $1.70.

### Key Points
- XRP peaked at $2.40 in January before declining over 50% to a June low of $1.02.
- Claude Fable 5 assigns a 50% probability to a base-case year-end price between $1.50 and $1.90.
- Bullish and bearish scenarios suggest potential year-end ranges of $2.40–$2.80 and $0.70–$0.90, respectively.
- Price performance remains heavily dependent on the CLARITY Act, Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, and Bitcoin market trends.
- Cumulative ETF inflows of $1.49 billion have provided a critical support floor for the token throughout the year.

### Why it Matters
The price of XRP remains highly sensitive to macroeconomic shifts and legislative developments regarding its legal status. Investors are closely monitoring these variables to determine if the asset can break its year-long downtrend or if it will face further downward pressure.
author: Sam Daodu

title: Tesla, SpaceX fall from record highs, Elon Musk lose trillionaire status: Profit-booking or re-rating of AI pricing?
summary:
Tesla and SpaceX shares have experienced significant declines, prompting investors to re-evaluate valuations for AI and space-sector companies amid broader market volatility and concerns over long-term profitability timelines.

### Key Points
- Tesla shares dropped approximately 8% despite reporting strong second-quarter vehicle delivery numbers.
- SpaceX stock faced a pullback following a strong market debut due to profit-taking and limited share availability.
- Market analysts suggest the decline reflects a broader re-rating of AI-linked valuations rather than fundamental business failures.
- Vested Finance CEO Viram Shah advises investors to focus on portfolio sizing rather than attempting to time market movements.
- Indian retail investors accessing US markets are cautioned that newly listed companies often experience high volatility during initial quarters.

### Why it Matters
This market correction highlights the risks associated with high-growth tech stocks that rely heavily on speculative future technologies like autonomy and AI. Investors should prioritize long-term thesis alignment and prudent position sizing to mitigate the impact of short-term price fluctuations in volatile sectors.
author: Sanchari Ghosh

title: Bookmark this now: These 2 Android sites could help you unbrick your Pixel
summary:
Google provides two official web-based tools, the Android Flash Tool and the Pixel Update and Software Repair site, to help users recover bricked or bootlooping Pixel smartphones.

### Key Points
- The Android Flash Tool allows users to flash factory images but requires an unlocked bootloader and results in a complete data wipe.
- The Pixel Update and Software Repair tool works on locked bootloaders and is designed to fix interrupted updates without erasing user data.
- Both tools utilize WebUSB technology and require the Google USB Driver for Windows users, while Mac, Linux, and Chrome OS users operate natively.
- Users must typically place their device into Fastboot mode by holding the volume down button during startup to ensure the tools detect the phone.
- The Pixel Repair site is recommended as a first resort for most users, while the Android Flash Tool is better suited for downgrading or deep system corruption.

### Why it Matters
These tools provide a critical safety net for Pixel owners who experience software failures or bootloops after installing Android updates. By offering accessible recovery options, Google reduces the need for professional repairs and helps users maintain device functionality without losing personal data.
author: Rita El Khoury
Boing Boing's Shop
summary:
FileJump is currently offering a lifetime subscription for 2TB of cloud storage at a discounted price of $59, providing a one-time payment alternative to recurring monthly subscription models.

### Key Points
- The lifetime subscription provides 2TB of storage space for a one-time fee of $59, significantly lower than the original $467 retail price.
- FileJump supports file uploads up to 15GB and includes integrated tools for editing Office documents directly within a web browser.
- Security features include optional zero-knowledge encryption, which protects files on the user's device before they are uploaded to the cloud.
- The service maintains a one-year file version history, allowing users to recover previous document iterations or revert accidental changes.
- Users can access their data via modern web browsers, a dedicated Android application, or WebDAV clients on Windows.

### Why it Matters
This offer presents a cost-effective alternative to standard subscription-based cloud services like Google One, which require ongoing monthly payments. By shifting to a lifetime model, users can potentially reduce long-term digital storage expenses while maintaining access to essential file management and security features.
title: 2TB cloud storage, yours forever on sale for $59

author: Tanveer Singh
summary:
The Nvidia RTX 3060 has solidified its status as the most popular graphics card among gamers, mirroring the legendary longevity and market dominance of the iconic GTX 1060.

### Key Points
- The GTX 1060 held the top spot on the Steam Hardware Survey for five years, from late 2017 through 2022.
- The RTX 3060 surpassed the GTX 1060 in early 2023 and has remained the most used GPU for the majority of the last three years.
- Key factors for the RTX 3060's popularity include its 12GB of VRAM and consistent performance in 1080p gaming.
- Newer models like the RTX 4060 and RTX 5060 are often criticized for having only 8GB of VRAM, which limits their appeal compared to the 3060.
- Nvidia’s 60-class and 50-class cards currently account for eight of the top ten most popular desktop GPUs on Steam.

### Why it Matters
The enduring popularity of the RTX 3060 highlights a growing trend where gamers are holding onto hardware longer due to rising prices and diminishing value in newer GPU generations. This shift suggests that mid-range cards with higher VRAM capacities provide better long-term utility than newer, more expensive models with lower memory specifications.
title: The RTX 3060 is becoming this decade's GTX 1060, but that's not a bad thing

author: Maham Fatima
summary:
CoStar Group has officially launched its commercial real estate intelligence platform in France, providing comprehensive market data and analytics to professionals across major hubs like Paris and Lyon.

### Key Points
- CoStar entered the €300 billion French commercial real estate market on July 2 using local acquisitions like BureauxLocaux and Business Immo.
- The platform tracks over 290,000 properties and 385,000 commercial tenants across the office, logistics, and hospitality sectors.
- Users gain access to verified lease and sale comparables, live property availabilities, and real-time market analytics.
- CEO Andy Florance stated the expansion aims to facilitate cross-border investment by connecting French assets to a global network of 320,000 subscribers.

### Why it Matters
This expansion marks a significant step in CoStar Group’s strategy to standardize global real estate data and increase market transparency in Europe. By providing advanced analytical tools to French industry professionals, the company strengthens its position as a primary information provider for international commercial property investors.
title: CoStar Group (CSGP): 10 Best NASDAQ Stocks to Invest In For Long Term

author: Mark Knapp
summary:
The Minisforum AtomMan G1 Pro is a compact 3.85-liter desktop PC featuring an AMD Ryzen 9 8945HX processor and Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 graphics for 1080p gaming performance.

### Key Points
- The system is available as a $1,299 barebones unit or a $1,799 pre-built model with 32GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD.
- Performance significantly improves when switching from the default "Gaming Mode" to "Beast Mode," yielding up to 38% higher frame rates in benchmarks.
- Hardware includes Wi-Fi 7, 5GbE networking, and a variety of display outputs, though it lacks high-speed USB4 or 20Gbps ports.
- The chassis design is compact but lacks dust filters, and internal components like the GPU and memory are difficult to access for future upgrades.
- Windows Defender flagged a vulnerable driver, Winring0, within the pre-installed Minisforum software, which may require user attention for security.

### Why it Matters
The AtomMan G1 Pro occupies a niche market for users who require a small-form-factor desktop but do not want the portability or constraints of a gaming laptop. While it offers decent performance, its price-to-performance ratio is challenged by larger, more powerful desktop towers that provide better cooling and easier upgrade paths.
title: Minisforum AtomMan G1 Pro Desktop Review: The Wobbly Line Between Desktop and True Mini PC

author: derrek.lee@futurenet.com (Derrek Lee) , Derrek Lee
summary:
The Oura Ring 5 introduces a significantly thinner, lighter design and improved battery life, solidifying its position as a leading wearable for passive health tracking and daily wellness monitoring.

### Key Points
- The Oura Ring 5 features a slimmed-down profile weighing approximately 2 grams, making it more discreet than the previous Oura Ring 4.
- Battery performance has increased to between six and nine days per charge, despite the device being 40% smaller than its predecessor.
- The ring includes advanced sensors for heart rate, blood oxygen, and temperature, though workout-specific heart rate tracking remains less accurate than dedicated fitness watches.
- New software features include an AI-powered Oura Advisor for health insights and a "Locate" tool to help users find their ring via Bluetooth proximity.
- The device is water-resistant up to 100 meters and supports integration with Apple Health and Android Health Connect.

### Why it Matters
The Oura Ring 5 represents a significant step forward in wearable miniaturization, proving that smart technology can be both unobtrusive and highly functional for long-term health monitoring. While the reliance on a subscription model and limitations in high-intensity fitness tracking persist, the device sets a new standard for comfort and design in the smart ring market.
title: I tested the Oura Ring 5 for a month, and it's exactly what other smart rings should aspire to be

author: desire.athow@futurenet.com (Desire Athow) , Desire Athow
summary:
Enterprises are struggling to manage "shadow AI" as employees increasingly bypass corporate security protocols to use unmanaged personal AI tools for improved productivity and faster task completion.

### Key Points
- Research from Teramind indicates that 67% of enterprise AI usage occurs through unmanaged personal accounts rather than company-provided software.
- Approximately 86% of organizations currently lack the necessary visibility to track how sensitive data moves to and from various AI platforms.
- Nearly 70% of C-suite executives admit to prioritizing speed over security when utilizing AI tools to meet competitive pressures.
- Traditional data loss prevention (DLP) tools often fail to detect shadow AI because they monitor file transfers rather than semantic data processed in chat prompts.
- Experts recommend a 90-day strategy focused on behavioral telemetry and "paved road" enablement to bring shadow AI usage under organizational governance.

### Why it Matters
The rise of shadow AI creates significant security vulnerabilities as sensitive corporate data is frequently pasted into unvetted, third-party chat interfaces. Organizations must shift from restrictive policies to agile, enablement-focused strategies to ensure that productivity gains do not come at the expense of data integrity.
title: ‘You fix it by making the secure option just as fast and frictionless as the risky one’: Practical advice on addressing shadow AI

author: Robert Triggs
summary:
YouTuber PewDiePie has released Odysseus, a privacy-focused, self-hosted AI workspace that allows users to manage local models, automate tasks, and maintain control over their personal data and documents.

### Key Points
- Odysseus is designed for self-hosting via Docker, ensuring user data remains local rather than being stored by third-party providers.
- The platform features a "Cookbook" interface that helps users select and manage AI models from Hugging Face based on their specific hardware capabilities.
- Users can integrate external cloud-hosted models through API keys from services like OpenRouter to supplement local processing power.
- Built-in tools include deep research capabilities, document co-editing, and a "Persona" system for creating custom, reusable AI system prompts.
- The software supports self-learning features, allowing agents to build memories of user preferences and refine their own skill sets over time.

### Why it Matters
Odysseus represents a growing shift toward local, transparent AI control, offering a viable alternative to subscription-based services like ChatGPT or Gemini. By prioritizing data privacy and self-hosted infrastructure, it provides power users with a customizable, agentic workspace that avoids the limitations and security concerns of centralized cloud platforms.
title: I self-hosted PewDiePie’s Odysseus AI workspace, and it’s surprisingly brilliant

author: Arin Waichulis
summary:
Apple advises against using sliding webcam covers on MacBooks because they can cause permanent display damage while providing no meaningful security benefits for modern hardware with integrated privacy indicators.

### Key Points
- Apple warns that closing a MacBook with a webcam cover thicker than 0.1 mm can crack the display due to tight hinge tolerances.
- Modern Macs feature a hardware-level circuit that forces the green privacy LED to illuminate whenever the camera sensor receives power.
- The hardware-linked indicator design, implemented in all Macs since late 2008, prevents malware from activating the camera without alerting the user.
- Security researcher Patrick Wardle developed the OverSight tool to provide additional alerts whenever the webcam is actively in use.
- Using webcam covers can interfere with ambient light sensors, potentially causing features like True Tone to malfunction.

### Why it Matters
These findings highlight that physical privacy accessories often pose a greater risk to hardware integrity than they do to digital security. Users should rely on built-in macOS security features and software monitoring tools rather than potentially damaging physical modifications.
title: Security Bite: A note on camera covers in 2026

author: pIat0n
summary:
A new bare-metal x86 tool enables users to perform cold boot attacks by dumping system RAM directly to a USB drive via legacy BIOS interrupts and unreal mode.

### Key Points
- The tool operates without an operating system by booting directly from a USB drive using a custom 512-byte boot sector.
- It utilizes BIOS INT 0x15 E820 to map physical memory and INT 0x13 to write 32KB chunks of RAM to the boot medium.
- Users must enable Legacy BIOS or Compatibility Support Module (CSM) settings on the target machine to execute the memory dump.
- The software requires NASM for compilation and overwrites data on the target USB drive starting at Logical Block Address (LBA) 64.
- This utility is designed for security research, specifically for extracting sensitive information like encryption keys from frozen memory modules.

### Why it Matters
This tool demonstrates the persistent security risks associated with physical memory access and the vulnerability of data stored in RAM during cold boot scenarios. It serves as a practical resource for security researchers to test system defenses against hardware-level memory extraction techniques.
title: BareMetal RAM Dumper – Bare-metal x86 tool for Cold Boot Attack experiments

author: Editorial Team
summary:
WeRide and Uber have announced a partnership to launch commercial autonomous robotaxi services in the Greater Zurich Region later this year, marking a significant expansion into the European market.

### Key Points
- WeRide and Uber plan to launch autonomous ride-hailing services in Zurich, pending approval from Switzerland’s Federal Roads Office.
- The partnership aims to achieve fully driverless operations in both Zurich and Madrid by mid-2027.
- Initial deployments in Zurich will include safety operators, with the transition to fully autonomous vehicles expected within approximately one year.
- Zurich is the fifth city activated under a global agreement between the two companies that covers 15 cities.
- Riders will access the autonomous fleet exclusively through the existing Uber mobile application.

### Why it Matters
This partnership highlights Uber’s strategic shift toward becoming a platform for third-party autonomous technology rather than developing its own proprietary systems. By integrating WeRide’s Level 4 technology, Uber aims to improve long-term unit economics by reducing reliance on human drivers while navigating complex European regulatory environments.
title: WeRide and Uber launch commercial robotaxi service in Zurich, expanding autonomous vehicle push across Europe

author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
summary:
North Korean threat actors are actively compromising software supply chains through the PolinRider campaign, which uses malicious packages and VS Code tasks to distribute malware to unsuspecting developers.

### Key Points
- The PolinRider campaign has deployed 108 unique malicious packages and extensions across npm, Packagist, Go, and Google Chrome.
- Attackers have compromised 1,951 public GitHub repositories by exploiting maintainer accounts and injecting obfuscated JavaScript loaders.
- Malicious VS Code task files are used to trigger arbitrary code execution when developers open infected folders in IDEs like VS Code or Cursor.
- The campaign delivers second-stage payloads, including the DEV#POPPER RAT and OmniStealer, by fetching encrypted data from blockchain infrastructure.
- Threat actors use Git history rewriting and anti-dated commits to disguise malicious changes as legitimate, long-standing repository updates.

### Why it Matters
This campaign highlights a significant escalation in supply chain attacks that target developer environments rather than just end-user applications. By compromising trusted repositories and IDE configurations, these actors can bypass traditional security measures and gain persistent access to sensitive development infrastructure.
title: North Korean Hackers Publish 108 Malicious Packages and Extensions in PolinRider Campaign

author: Yves Smith
summary:
The Israel Defense Forces have expanded their operational control to 70% of the Gaza Strip, while global markets face mounting instability driven by AI bubble fears and economic volatility.

### Key Points
- IDF control in Gaza has increased from 53% to 70% of the territory despite ongoing ceasefire negotiations.
- Retail investors are purchasing S&P 500 equities at 3.5 times the daily average, marking a record high since 2020.
- The U.S. military has deployed additional combat units to the Middle East, bringing total regional force levels to approximately 10,000 personnel.
- New data indicates that average new car prices in the United States have reached a record high of $51,974.
- Google’s AI Overviews have faced scrutiny for generating authoritative but inaccurate information during high-profile investigations.

### Why it Matters
The convergence of escalating geopolitical conflicts and extreme financial speculation in the AI sector creates a precarious environment for global markets. These developments suggest that both institutional and retail investors are increasingly vulnerable to sudden shifts in regional stability and economic policy.
title: Links 7/4/2026

author: Shaheer Khan
summary:
Understanding the color-coding system for USB-A ports helps users identify data transfer speeds and power capabilities, though manufacturer inconsistencies often require consulting device manuals for accurate technical specifications.

### Key Points
- White ports indicate the original USB 1.0 standard, while black ports represent the faster USB 2.0 generation introduced in 2000.
- Blue ports signify USB 3.0, offering data speeds up to 5Gbps, whereas teal or red ports typically denote the 10Gbps USB 3.1 Gen 2 standard.
- Yellow or orange USB-A ports feature "Always-on" charging, allowing devices to charge even when the host computer is powered down.
- Manufacturers sometimes ignore standard color conventions for aesthetic reasons, such as matching ports to a motherboard's specific color theme.
- Users should reserve high-speed USB 3.0 and newer ports for external drives, while using older ports for low-bandwidth peripherals like mice or keyboards.

### Why it Matters
Properly identifying USB-A port capabilities ensures that high-performance hardware, such as external SSDs, receives the necessary bandwidth for optimal operation. Relying on visual cues alone can be misleading, so verifying port specifications through official documentation prevents performance bottlenecks and hardware compatibility issues.
title: I didn't know USB port colors meant something — now I plug devices into the right one every time

author: MacRumors Staff
summary:
Apple is navigating a series of product rumors, including the upcoming MacBook Ultra and iPhone 18 lineup, alongside a significant data breach involving manufacturing partner Tata in India.

### Key Points
- The rumored touchscreen MacBook Ultra will reportedly feature M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than newer M6 or M7 silicon.
- Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo expects the 2027 iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e to include 9GB of RAM and the A20 processor.
- A cyberattack on Apple supplier Tata resulted in the leak of confidential documents regarding iPhone 18 Pro components on the dark web.
- Apple released iOS 26.5.2, iPadOS, and macOS Tahoe updates to address more than 25 critical security vulnerabilities.
- The company acquired assets and talent from Rabbit 3 Times, the developer behind the award-winning app design tool Play.

### Why it Matters
These developments highlight Apple's ongoing struggle to balance rapid hardware innovation with the security risks posed by its global supply chain. Potential price increases and data leaks could impact consumer trust and market positioning as the company prepares for its next generation of flagship devices.
title: Top Stories: 'MacBook Ultra' and iPhone 18 Rumors, iOS 26.5.2 Security Fixes, and More

author: Sponsored Post
summary:
The Zawa all-in-one AI design platform enables small business owners to generate professional logos, brand identities, and marketing content without requiring prior design experience or expensive software outsourcing.

### Key Points
- Zawa uses AI to generate customizable logos based on specific business names, industries, and user-defined style preferences.
- The platform includes a full studio suite for creating brand guidelines, social media content, and website assets.
- Integrated image tools offer 4K resolution enhancement, 8x enlarging, background removal, and object removal capabilities.
- AI agents can process complex design prompts in the background to automate branding tasks and content creation.
- Video features include low-resolution clip enhancement, watermark removal, and the generation of new product videos.
- Subscription plans for the platform start at less than $6 per month when billed annually.

### Why it Matters
This platform lowers the barrier to entry for entrepreneurs by consolidating essential branding and design tools into a single, cost-effective workflow. By automating complex visual tasks, Zawa allows small businesses to maintain professional standards while significantly reducing the time and capital typically required for creative production.
title: Zawa is your one-stop shop for building your brand with logo & image tools, more

author: mhuck@live.com (Mauro Huculak) , Mauro Huculak
summary:
Windows 11 users can restrict total system memory for testing and debugging purposes by adjusting the Maximum memory setting within the legacy System Configuration tool, also known as msconfig.

### Key Points
- Access the memory limit setting by searching for "msconfig" and navigating to the Boot tab's Advanced options.
- Users must input the desired memory limit in megabytes, such as 4096 for 4GB or 8192 for 8GB.
- A system restart is required to apply the memory restriction or to restore full RAM access.
- Modern systems with UEFI firmware and Secure Boot enabled may require temporarily disabling security features to modify these settings.
- This configuration is strictly for testing or troubleshooting and is not recommended for improving everyday system performance.

### Why it Matters
Artificially limiting RAM is a specialized diagnostic technique used by developers and IT professionals to simulate low-memory environments without hardware changes. Using this setting for general use is counterproductive, as it significantly degrades system performance and restricts the operating system's ability to manage resources efficiently.
title: I found a hidden way to limit RAM on Windows 11, and the results were way more surprising than I expected

author: Ana Maria Constantin
summary:
Hong Kong has emerged as a critical semiconductor hub, handling over half of China’s $239 billion in chip imports during the first five months of 2026 amid rising AI demand.

### Key Points
- Hong Kong re-exported $124 billion worth of semiconductors to mainland China between January and May 2026.
- AI-related electronics now comprise between 57% and 70% of the city's total exports, fueling a 5.9% economic growth rate in the first quarter.
- The city’s free-port status and advanced air cargo infrastructure allow it to outperform mainland ports in handling high-value, time-sensitive technology goods.
- Hong Kong has become Taiwan’s largest chip export market, surpassing direct shipments to the Chinese mainland.
- The Hong Kong Trade Development Council recently doubled its 2026 export growth forecast to over 20% due to the ongoing technology upcycle.

### Why it Matters
Hong Kong’s role as a primary intermediary for high-tech trade highlights its strategic importance in the global AI supply chain despite increasing geopolitical friction between the US and China. This reliance on transshipment leaves the city vulnerable to tightening international export controls and ongoing scrutiny regarding the movement of restricted semiconductor technologies.
title: Hong Kong now handles more than half of China’s chip imports

author: Helene Braun
summary:
Bitcoin is currently trading below $62,000 as analysts from Charles Schwab and Hashdex suggest that capital rotation into AI stocks and historical halving cycles explain the recent price disconnect.

### Key Points
- Bitcoin prices remain down over 50% from October peaks while U.S. technology stocks reach record highs due to AI-driven investor interest.
- Hashdex CIO Samir Kerbage attributes the crypto slump to capital shifting toward AI infrastructure, IPOs, and macroeconomic rate expectations.
- On-chain activity remains strong, with stablecoin transaction volumes in the first half of the year already exceeding the total volume recorded in 2025.
- Charles Schwab researcher Jim Ferraioli notes that bitcoin’s current recovery aligns with historical post-halving cycles rather than a fundamental breakdown.
- Estimates suggest the average investor cost basis is near $80,000, creating potential selling pressure as holders look to exit positions after recovering losses.

### Why it Matters
The current divergence between bitcoin's price and its underlying network activity suggests a potential market correction as institutional infrastructure continues to expand. Investors are closely watching whether historical halving patterns will hold or if shifting capital flows toward AI will permanently alter the cryptocurrency's traditional growth cycle.
title: Why bitcoin's disconnect from record-high stocks won't last

author: Pierluigi Paganini
title: FBI: TeamPCP Compromised Dev Tools to Steal Cloud Credentials
summary:
The FBI issued a FLASH alert on July 2, 2026, warning that the criminal group TeamPCP is compromising developer tools to execute large-scale software supply chain attacks.

### Key Points
- TeamPCP injected malicious code into widely used tools including Trivy, KICS, LiteLLM, and the Telnyx Python SDK.
- The group deployed four malware families—CanisterWorm, SANDCLOCK, Mini Shai-Hulud, and Miasma—to harvest cloud tokens, SSH keys, and Kubernetes secrets.
- Attackers gained control of npm accounts by registering expired recovery email domains linked to package maintainers.
- The campaign is associated with four specific CVEs: CVE-2026-33634, CVE-2026-48027, CVE-2026-45321, and CVE-2025-55182.
- Recommended mitigations include pinning GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, enforcing phishing-resistant MFA, and rotating all CI/CD secrets.

### Why it Matters
This campaign demonstrates how attackers can bypass traditional security by poisoning the trusted tools and pipelines that organizations rely on for software development. Because the stolen credentials may be shared with other criminal groups, impacted organizations must treat all exposed data as a persistent, long-term security risk.

author: View Archive →
title: Soatok's Informal Guide to Threat Models
summary:
Effective threat modeling requires identifying assets, potential adversaries, and attack vectors while clearly documenting system assumptions to build more resilient and secure software architectures.

### Key Points
- A functional threat model must define protected assets, identify potential actors, map attack scenarios, and outline specific prevention or mitigation strategies.
- Effective models are living documents that explicitly state assumptions and acknowledge risks that the development team chooses not to address.
- Visualizing system components as a graph helps identify inappropriate dependencies and potential security blind spots during the design phase.
- Poorly constructed threat models often lack lists of assumptions or asset relationships, rendering them ineffective for actual security analysis.
- Applying threat modeling to technical debates, such as post-quantum cryptography standards, helps distinguish between legitimate security concerns and ideological fearmongering.

### Why it Matters
Understanding threat modeling allows developers to move beyond buzzwords and proactively design systems that force attackers into predictable, mitigated paths. By identifying and documenting assumptions early, teams can avoid architectural flaws that are difficult or impossible to patch after a product is deployed.

author: Aditi Bharade,Henry Chandonnet
title: Tokenmaxxing is so over. It's all about modelmaxxing now.
summary:
Companies are shifting away from "tokenmaxxing" by adopting model switching, a cost-saving strategy that routes complex tasks to premium AI models while offloading simpler work to cheaper alternatives.

### Key Points
- Tech companies are moving from unlimited AI usage to strategic "token hygiene" to manage rising API costs and budget constraints.
- Professionals are using design-first workflows and model routing tools to optimize performance and reduce unnecessary token consumption.
- Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong predicts that 80% of AI workloads will transition to significantly cheaper models within the next 12 to 18 months.
- Adoption of model routing platforms, such as OpenRouter and Rayline, has increased from 1% to 5% of firms over the past year.
- Behavioral economists note that strict token budgets create a scarcity mindset, encouraging users to be more selective about which AI models they employ.

### Why it Matters
This transition signals a maturing AI market where efficiency and cost-optimization are replacing the initial "hype-driven" phase of unrestricted usage. By strategically matching model intelligence to task complexity, businesses can maintain high productivity while significantly reducing their operational overhead.

author: Fergus Gregg
title: Trump made huge profits from his crypto. Did anyone else?
summary:
US President Donald Trump generated $1.4 billion in income from cryptocurrency ventures over the past year, primarily driven by royalties and token sales from his branded meme coins.

### Key Points
- President Trump earned $635 million from meme coin royalties and $236 million from token sales, largely linked to the $TRUMP cryptocurrency.
- The $TRUMP coin value peaked at nearly $75 per unit before falling to $1.65 by July 2026.
- Senator Adam Schiff and other lawmakers are investigating potential market manipulation and the loss of an estimated $4.3 billion in retail investor wealth.
- Reports indicate that 45 "early-deployment" wallets earned $1.2 billion, resulting in a ratio where retail investors lost $20 for every dollar gained by insiders.
- World Liberty Financial, managed by Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr., facilitated additional income and launched the USD1 stablecoin in May 2025.

### Why it Matters
The significant financial losses suffered by retail investors compared to the gains of insiders highlight the extreme volatility and regulatory risks associated with meme coins. This situation has prompted congressional scrutiny into the intersection of political influence and speculative digital asset markets.

author: Cointelegraph by Marcel Pechman
title: SOL rallies as Solana memecoins, prediction market activity surge: Are bulls back?
summary:
Solana’s native token SOL reached a 30-day high of $83, driven by increased activity in network-based memecoins, tokenized assets, and the launch of new decentralized prediction market platforms.

### Key Points
- SOL reached a 30-day high of $83 on Friday, decoupling from the broader altcoin market's recent downward trend.
- Tokenized assets on the Solana network hit a record $3.5 billion, led by corporate credit tokens and stock market indexes.
- The ANSEM memecoin, launched on Pump.fun, reached a $112 million market capitalization, while the PUMP token saw 27% weekly gains.
- New prediction market platforms, including World and Jupiter, launched on the network to compete for betting volume during the World Cup.
- Solana leads the tokenized industry with 294,274 active addresses, significantly outpacing Ethereum’s 204,955.
- SOL perpetual futures funding rates dropped to 3%, indicating that traders are currently hesitant to leverage positions for a rally toward $90.

### Why it Matters
The surge in Solana activity highlights a growing shift toward real-world asset tokenization and niche decentralized finance applications as primary drivers for network growth. However, the cooling of leveraged futures suggests that market participants remain cautious about whether these speculative trends can sustain long-term price appreciation.

author: Oswarld (Kwangseob Ahn)
title: Bloomberg Terminal Is Ugly and Clunky–Everyone Still Uses It
summary:
A social media post by Iran’s parliament speaker featuring a Bloomberg Terminal command has sparked speculation regarding potential sanctions evasion and the country's involvement in global oil trading.

### Key Points
- Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted the command "EUCRBRDT Index GP," which retrieves a real-time price chart for Brent crude oil on the Bloomberg Terminal.
- The Bloomberg Terminal is a closed, high-cost financial platform used by 350,000 professionals, with annual subscriptions costing approximately $32,000 per seat.
- Bloomberg maintains a dominant market position through structural "lock-in," including proprietary data, benchmark indices, and the IB chat network used for trade execution.
- The platform is integrating generative AI through BloombergGPT, focusing on folding advanced analytics into existing workflows rather than creating standalone tools.
- Despite its high cost and steep learning curve, the terminal remains the industry standard because it functions as essential infrastructure for global financial communication.

### Why it Matters
The incident highlights the Bloomberg Terminal's status as the indispensable "lingua franca" of global finance, where proprietary data and counterparty networks create a nearly impenetrable competitive moat. This structural reliance makes the platform difficult to replace, even for sanctioned entities that must navigate the same financial infrastructure as the rest of the world.

author: DealzRGood4U
title: 20L VEVOR/Succebuy 12V/24V DC 110-240V AC Fridge Portable Compressor Cooler $87 & More + Free S&H
summary:
AliExpress is offering VEVOR and Succebuy portable compressor coolers starting at $86.99, featuring dual-voltage compatibility and mobile app control for various outdoor activities and home use.

### Key Points
- Prices start at $86.99 for the 20L model after applying specific promo codes at checkout.
- Available sizes include 20L, 22L, 35L, and 55L capacities with free shipping from a USA warehouse.
- Units operate on 12V/24V DC or 110-240V AC power with a temperature range of -4°F to 68°F.
- Features include a smart touch panel, mobile app connectivity, and a three-level battery protection system.
- The 20L model consumes 60W of power and maintains noise levels at or below 45dB.

### Why it Matters
These portable coolers provide a versatile, energy-efficient refrigeration solution for travelers and outdoor enthusiasts who require reliable temperature control on the go. The dual-voltage functionality and battery protection features make these units particularly useful for road trips and camping where power sources may be inconsistent.

author: Zoe Skyforest
title: Building A Wireless Fingerprint Authorization Device
summary:
The immurok is a custom-built, wireless biometric authentication device designed to streamline terminal workflows and system logins for Linux and Mac users by replacing manual password entry with fingerprints.

### Key Points
- The device utilizes a WCH CH592F microcontroller for Bluetooth connectivity and an R559S capacitive sensor for local biometric verification.
- It functions as a standard Bluetooth HID keyboard, ensuring compatibility across different operating systems without transmitting sensitive biometric data.
- Linux integration relies on a CLI/TUI application and PAM to manage system logins and sudo terminal commands.
- Mac users can utilize a dedicated menu bar application and PAM integration to handle administrative prompts and lock screen authentication.

### Why it Matters
This project offers a practical solution for power users who frequently encounter repetitive password prompts during terminal-heavy workflows. By bringing mobile-style biometric convenience to desktop environments, it demonstrates how custom hardware can effectively bridge gaps in existing operating system security interfaces.

author: staff@bgr.com (Alvin Wanjala)
title: 5 Discontinued Apple Products That Are Still Worth Buying In 2026
summary:
Despite being discontinued, several older Apple devices remain functional and cost-effective options for consumers looking to save money on reliable technology in the current 2026 market.

### Key Points
- The 2018 iPad Pro 12.9-inch (3rd gen) features a 120 Hz Liquid Retina display and was the first Apple tablet to adopt USB-C connectivity.
- The 2019 13-inch MacBook Pro remains viable for basic tasks and is notable for being the final model to feature Apple's butterfly keyboard.
- The iPhone 11 Pro supports iOS 26 and offers a versatile triple-camera system, providing a budget-friendly alternative to modern 5G-enabled smartphones.
- The iPod classic has seen a resurgence due to its offline music capabilities and a modding community that enables modern upgrades like Bluetooth and SSD storage.
- The Apple Watch Series 5 includes an Always-On display and essential health tracking features, making it a capable entry-level wearable for fitness monitoring.
- These vintage devices are widely available on secondary marketplaces like Amazon, Best Buy, and eBay, with prices typically ranging from $100 to $300.

### Why it Matters
Purchasing discontinued Apple hardware allows budget-conscious consumers to access high-quality technology at a fraction of the cost of current-generation models. These devices demonstrate the long-term durability of Apple's ecosystem, offering continued utility for basic computing, media consumption, and connectivity needs.

author: harish.jonnalagadda@futurenet.com (Harish Jonnalagadda) , Harish Jonnalagadda
title: Prime Day is done, but this best-selling 4K projector is still at its lowest price
summary:
The XGIMI Horizon 20 Max is currently the top-rated 4K long-throw projector, offering significant improvements in brightness, ease of setup, and image quality for a discounted price of $2,199.

### Key Points
- The Horizon 20 Max features a built-in gimbal and optical zoom, allowing for flexible placement and easy screen alignment.
- It delivers up to 5,700 lumens of brightness, ensuring vibrant image quality even in rooms with significant ambient light.
- The device is powered by the MediaTek MT9679 platform with 4GB of RAM and 128GB of storage for a smooth Google TV experience.
- Connectivity options include Wi-Fi 6, dual HDMI ports with eARC, and support for Dolby Vision and IMAX Enhanced formats.
- XGIMI has discounted the projector to $2,199 for the Fourth of July, marking its lowest price point to date.

### Why it Matters
This projector simplifies the home theater experience by removing the technical barriers typically associated with installing long-throw hardware. Its high brightness and automated setup features make it a versatile option for users who want a premium, large-screen viewing experience without needing a dedicated dark room.

author: BeauHD
title: Alibaba To Ban Claude Code In Workplace Over Alleged Backdoor Risks
summary:
Alibaba has officially banned employees from using Anthropic’s Claude Code tool, directing staff to its internal Qoder platform following allegations of unauthorized model distillation and data security disputes.

### Key Points
- Anthropic accused Alibaba of illicitly extracting its AI model capabilities through a process known as distillation to accelerate Chinese development.
- Claude Code includes mechanisms that inspect user environments, such as timezones and proxy data, to identify and restrict unauthorized access.
- Anthropic stated these tracking features were launched in March to prevent account abuse and protect its proprietary technology from being copied.
- Alibaba’s internal directive mandates that employees transition to the company's proprietary Qoder platform for their development needs.
- The dispute highlights ongoing geopolitical tensions and the intense competition between U.S. and Chinese firms to lead in artificial intelligence innovation.

### Why it Matters
This conflict underscores the growing legal and compliance risks companies face as they attempt to protect advanced AI models from unauthorized international replication. It also illustrates the technical challenges firms encounter when trying to enforce regional usage restrictions in an increasingly globalized digital infrastructure.

author: Dr. Tim Sandle
title: Cybersecurity in space: Protecting the next frontier of critical infrastructure
summary:
Cybersecurity experts are warning that the rapid expansion of space-based infrastructure requires new autonomous defense strategies, as satellites and orbital systems face unique, unpatchable vulnerabilities to cyberattacks.

### Key Points
- Cybersecurity firm OPSWAT successfully tested its MetaDefender Kiosk in near-space conditions, demonstrating the potential for autonomous, offline file sanitization in extreme environments.
- Space-based assets, including GPS, telecommunications, and financial networks, are increasingly classified as critical infrastructure vulnerable to jamming, signal spoofing, and ransomware.
- The World Economic Forum’s Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026 highlights that organizations are now integrating space-based asset risks into their formal cyber defense planning.
- Future orbital data centers and satellite constellations require zero-trust architectures that prioritize prevention over traditional, human-led patching and monitoring.
- Canada is prioritizing space resilience as companies like Telesat expand low-Earth orbit networks, necessitating advanced security against nation-state and criminal cyber threats.

### Why it Matters
As global reliance on space-based systems grows, the inability to physically repair or manually patch orbital hardware creates a significant security gap. Developing autonomous, prevention-first cybersecurity is essential to protecting the critical infrastructure that supports modern telecommunications, military operations, and global financial stability.

author: Sachin  Gupta
title: The new economics of agri warehousing: Securing assets, securing returns
summary:
Modern agricultural warehousing is evolving from passive storage into a dynamic financial hub, utilizing digital oversight and AI-driven quality assessment to transform physical commodities into secure, liquid assets.

### Key Points
- Traditional agricultural supply chains face high financing costs due to inventory opacity, quality degradation, and risks associated with collateral verification.
- The new economic model integrates scientific storage controls to minimize post-harvest spoilage and maintain the long-term market value of commodities.
- Real-time digital surveillance and automated audit systems provide lenders with immutable, transparent data to reduce non-performing asset risks.
- AI and machine learning tools replace manual sampling to provide objective, standardized quality reports for specific commodity lots.
- Enhanced risk visibility allows financial institutions to offer competitive warehouse receipt financing to smallholders, traders, and mid-tier processors.

### Why it Matters
This shift enables agricultural commodities to function as reliable, financeable collateral, bridging the gap between rural producers and urban capital markets. By reducing systemic risk, the model stabilizes commodity prices and provides essential liquidity to the agricultural sector, fostering a more efficient and sustainable financial ecosystem.

author: CryptoProwl
title: Weekly Wrap: Crypto Recovers To Start Third Quarter
summary:
Cryptocurrency markets are showing signs of recovery as Bitcoin and Ethereum prices rise following a significant influx of capital into spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds in early July.

### Key Points
- Bitcoin ETFs recorded $221.7 million in inflows on July 2, ending a 10-day streak of $2.73 billion in total outflows.
- Ethereum prices increased by 3% to $1,740 as investors rotated capital away from semiconductor stocks like Micron Technology.
- Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest purchased $75 million in crypto-related stocks during June, including $44 million in Coinbase Global shares.
- Cryptocurrency firms have spent $189 million on U.S. midterm election influence, accounting for over one-third of total corporate political spending.
- Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald project the current "crypto winter" will likely reach a market bottom by late October.

### Why it Matters
The recent rebound suggests a shift in investor sentiment as capital flows back into digital assets following a period of significant market volatility. This trend, combined with increased political lobbying and institutional adoption, indicates that the cryptocurrency sector is positioning itself for a potential recovery in the coming months.

author: Scott Webster
title: Motorola Razr Ultra (2026) Review
summary:
The Motorola Razr Ultra (2026) offers a highly polished flip phone experience with premium materials and class-leading battery life, though its $1,499 price tag makes it a difficult recommendation.

### Key Points
- The device features a 4-inch external cover display that supports full Android app functionality and a 7-inch 165Hz internal AMOLED screen.
- Hardware includes a Snapdragon 8 Elite processor, 16GB of RAM, 512GB of storage, and a 5,000mAh silicon-carbon battery.
- The design incorporates a titanium-reinforced hinge, IP48 water and dust resistance, and unique finishes like Alcantara and real wood.
- Motorola promises three years of Android OS upgrades and five years of security updates, which trails behind competitors offering seven-year support.
- The primary 50MP camera utilizes a new LOFIC sensor to improve dynamic range, though software image processing still requires further refinement.

### Why it Matters
The Razr Ultra represents a mature, high-quality foldable that excels in daily usability but struggles to justify its premium price point against competitors with longer software support. While the hardware is top-tier, the device faces a challenging market position that makes it a much more attractive option once retail discounts are applied.

author: Michail
title: iPhone 18 Pro leaks, Redmi K90 Ultra arrives, Week 27 in review
summary:
Apple is preparing for its September 8, 2026, launch event, featuring the new iPhone 18 Pro series, the foldable iPhone Ultra, and significant battery capacity upgrades for flagship models.

### Key Points
- The iPhone 18 Pro Max will feature a 5,235 mAh battery for physical SIM models and a 5,425 mAh capacity for eSIM versions.
- Xiaomi announced the Redmi K90 Ultra in China, featuring a Snapdragon 8 Elite chipset, 165Hz AMOLED display, and an 8,550mAh battery.
- Nothing is scheduled to launch its Phone (4b) on July 7, which will include a 6,000 mAh battery and a Snapdragon 6 Gen 4 processor.
- The OnePlus N6 launched in India for INR 22,999, boasting an 8,000mAh battery and a seven-year battery health guarantee.
- Leaked documents from an Apple supplier cyberattack suggest the iPhone 18 Pro series will utilize a mix of Qualcomm and proprietary Apple C2 modems.

### Why it Matters
These hardware developments highlight a growing industry trend toward significantly larger battery capacities and extended device longevity to support intensive mobile gaming and daily usage. As manufacturers like Apple, Xiaomi, and Nothing compete for market share, these technical specifications will likely influence consumer purchasing decisions throughout the second half of 2026.

author: Brady Snyder
title: I make these 3 tweaks to every pair of earbuds I buy — they all sound better than stock
summary:
Users can significantly improve the audio quality of their wireless earbuds by manually adjusting Bluetooth codecs, applying custom equalizer settings, and carefully managing spatial audio features on Android.

### Key Points
- Enable high-resolution Bluetooth codecs like LDAC or LHDC via Android's Developer options to bypass the bitrate limitations of standard SBC or AAC.
- Use the Wavelet app to apply AutoEQ presets, which adjust frequency response curves to match the scientifically backed Harman Curve.
- Access Developer options by tapping the build number seven times in the Android Settings menu to unlock advanced Bluetooth audio codec selection.
- Evaluate spatial audio and Dolby Atmos settings carefully, as these features can sometimes reduce audio detail compared to standard stereo playback.
- Ensure streaming services are configured for lossless audio to maintain high-fidelity quality throughout the entire playback chain.

### Why it Matters
Optimizing these hidden software settings allows users to extract superior performance from their existing hardware without purchasing new equipment. By moving beyond default manufacturer profiles, listeners can achieve a personalized audio experience that better aligns with their specific hearing preferences and high-resolution source material.

author: Piyush Gupta
title: Godot bans "vibe-coded" code contributions
summary:
The Godot game engine development team is updating its contribution policy to strictly prohibit AI-generated code, citing concerns over code quality and the inability of contributors to maintain submissions.

### Key Points
- Godot maintainers are banning autonomous AI-authored code and "vibe-coded" contributions to prevent repository clutter.
- New contributors with three or fewer merged pull requests must now obtain explicit permission before submitting significant features or refactoring.
- AI usage is restricted to menial tasks like code completion or regex, and any AI assistance must be disclosed in pull request discussions.
- Communication channels will be restricted to human-to-human interaction, explicitly banning AI agents and bots from participating in discussions.
- The team stated that AI-generated pull requests are demoralizing and create an unsustainable burden for maintainers who must review and fix the code.

### Why it Matters
This policy shift highlights a growing tension between open-source maintainers and the influx of automated code contributions that lack human oversight. By prioritizing code comprehension and accountability, Godot is setting a precedent for how major software projects may restrict AI tools to preserve long-term project stability and developer morale.

author: Ross Rubin
title: PC makers are chasing 'creatives'. But who are they?
summary:
PC manufacturers like Acer and Asus are increasingly tailoring high-performance hardware configurations to meet the specific aesthetic and functional demands of professional content creators over traditional gaming designs.

### Key Points
- PC makers are shifting from gaming-centric branding to creator-focused lines like Asus ProArt, which prioritize minimalist aesthetics and color-accurate displays.
- Creative professionals require high-performance GPUs, significant system memory, and fast storage to handle modern generative AI workflows and video editing.
- Small form factor desktops are gaining traction for professional use, with companies like Asus and Acer integrating advanced AI-ready architectures into compact chassis.
- Local AI model execution, such as video generation via LTX or Wan, necessitates hardware with at least 12 GB of VRAM and substantial SSD capacity.
- Industry leaders note that while gaming and creative hardware share core components, creators prefer subdued designs that avoid the "flashy" RGB lighting common in gaming PCs.

### Why it Matters
The convergence of gaming-grade performance and professional-grade design reflects a broader market shift toward hardware that supports resource-intensive generative AI tasks locally.
