author: Dan Goodin, Ars Technica
title: A Critical Deadline Is Approaching for Windows and Linux Security

summary:
Modern antivirus software is shifting from signature-based detection to AI-driven behavioral analysis, allowing security platforms to identify and block evolving cyber threats before they can execute on a system.

### Key Points
- Traditional antivirus relied on databases of known malware signatures, which struggle to keep pace with polymorphic and metamorphic malware.
- Modern security tools utilize machine learning, neural networks, and decision trees to classify files based on suspicious behavior rather than identity.
- Behavioral analysis monitors real-time activities like API calls, memory access, and unauthorized encryption to detect threats like ransomware.
- Sandboxing and dynamic analysis allow software to safely execute suspicious files in isolated environments to observe their actions before granting system access.
- Major security providers, including Microsoft, CrowdStrike, and SentinelOne, are increasingly integrating these predictive capabilities into their platforms.

### Why it Matters
This transition represents a fundamental change in how devices defend against zero-day attacks that have no prior record in security databases. While these AI-driven tools significantly improve proactive protection, users must still practice good digital hygiene, as modern cyberattacks often bypass software entirely by targeting human behavior through phishing and social engineering.
author: Marshall Gunnell
title: Malware Has Gotten Smarter. Here's How Your Antivirus Has, Too

summary:
InstaLILY AI is challenging the dominance of centralized cloud infrastructure by introducing a "Small Data Center" approach that prioritizes local, proprietary intelligence for industrial and operational workflows.

### Key Points
- InstaLILY AI launched a "Small Data Center" model that runs intelligence stacks locally to address latency and connectivity issues in industrial environments.
- The company claims its system reduced logistics routing times by 80% and cut field-team training time by 60% for industrial operators.
- The platform utilizes "InstaBrain" and "InstaWorkers" to execute tasks directly within existing systems while maintaining private governance.
- Distributed AI allows companies to own their operational intelligence, creating a compounding asset that improves as it learns from specific organizational workflows.
- Hyperscalers are hesitant to fully embrace distributed inference because it threatens the revenue models built around centralized cloud consumption.

### Why it Matters
The shift toward distributed AI infrastructure allows enterprises to move beyond generic cloud models and gain competitive advantages through proprietary, localized intelligence. By processing data closer to physical operations, companies can improve efficiency and security while reducing reliance on massive, energy-intensive data centers.
author: desire.athow@futurenet.com (Desire Athow) , Desire Athow
title: ‘The defining divide in enterprise software over the next five years will be between companies that rent intelligence versus companies that own it’: Enterprise AI is becoming increasingly distributed

summary:
Tech workers are increasingly dedicating significant personal time and money to mastering artificial intelligence tools outside of work hours to remain competitive in a rapidly evolving job market.

### Key Points
- An Ernst & Young survey found that 85% of US desk workers are learning to use AI tools during their personal time.
- Software engineers and product designers report spending 10 to 20 hours weekly on after-hours AI experimentation to avoid becoming technically obsolete.
- Professionals are paying out-of-pocket for subscriptions to tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor, with some spending thousands annually on training and software.
- LinkedIn data shows a surge in hiring for AI-specific engineering roles, while demand for traditional software engineering positions has remained flat or declined.
- Some employees, such as those at Amazon, report that internal company resources help, but heavy workloads still force most learning into evenings and weekends.

### Why it Matters
This trend highlights a growing "learning tax" where the burden of professional development shifts from employers to individual workers to keep pace with technological disruption. As AI continues to reshape industry standards, the ability to adapt quickly is becoming a critical factor in long-term job security and career advancement.
author: Jacob Zinkula
title: Tech workers are spending nights and weekends learning new AI tools. They say they can't afford not to.

summary:
Google is investigating widespread touchscreen issues, including dead zones and reversed scrolling, affecting Pixel 7, 8, 9, and 10 series devices following the recent Android 17 software update.

### Key Points
- Users report erratic touchscreen behavior, such as ignored taps and inverted scrolling, across the entire system interface.
- The bug impacts the modern Pixel lineup, specifically the Pixel 7, 8, 9, and 10 series smartphones.
- Google’s suggested fix of clearing the Pixel Launcher cache has yielded inconsistent results for affected users.
- Some owners report temporary relief by toggling the "Smooth Display" setting off and back on in the device menu.
- Google has not yet provided a definitive timeline for a permanent software patch to resolve these input errors.

### Why it Matters
This widespread bug significantly degrades the core functionality of Google's flagship hardware, rendering devices difficult to navigate for many users. The lack of a reliable, universal fix highlights the risks of early adoption for major OS updates and may impact consumer trust in the stability of the Pixel ecosystem.
author: techkritiko@gmail.com (Jay Bonggolto) , Jay Bonggolto
title: Android 17 is off to a rough start with new Pixel touchscreen complaints

summary:
A massive data leak exposed 74,000 Fortinet firewall credentials, while critical vulnerabilities in Splunk Enterprise and SimpleHelp RMM are currently being exploited by attackers in the wild.

### Key Points
- A Russian-speaking group leaked credentials from 74,000 Fortinet firewalls and VPN gateways after accidentally exposing them on a server.
- CISA added a critical, remotely exploitable vulnerability in Splunk Enterprise (CVE-2026-20253) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
- A critical flaw in the SimpleHelp RMM tool (CVE-2026-48558) allows unauthenticated attackers to gain full remote access to managed endpoints.
- Attackers are actively exploiting three vulnerabilities in FortiSandbox, a platform essential for threat blocking and automated security responses.
- Microsoft is developing a patch for a zero-day vulnerability in Defender (CVE-2026-50656) that enables local privilege escalation.

### Why it Matters
These incidents highlight a significant escalation in supply chain and infrastructure risks, as attackers increasingly target the management tools that organizations rely on for security. The widespread exposure of administrative credentials and active exploitation of RMM software demonstrate that even robust security perimeters are vulnerable when foundational management platforms are compromised.
author: Help Net Security
title: Week in review: 74k Fortinet firewall credentials stolen, Splunk Enterprise RCE under active attack

summary:
2024 Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu warns that current AI productivity projections are vastly overstated, arguing that the technology will likely only automate 5% of tasks over the next decade.

### Key Points
- MIT economist Daron Acemoglu estimates AI will contribute only 0.55% to total factor productivity growth over the next ten years.
- Acemoglu characterizes roughly 80% of current public discourse regarding artificial intelligence as speculative or intellectually unserious.
- The Nobel winner argues that policymakers should prioritize addressing corporate monopoly power and AI-driven labor displacement over abstract debates about capitalism.
- Acemoglu rejects the term "capitalism" as a useful economic descriptor, preferring his framework of inclusive versus extractive institutions to analyze national prosperity.

### Why it Matters
Acemoglu’s critique challenges the prevailing market optimism surrounding AI, suggesting that the technology's actual economic impact will be significantly more modest than Wall Street forecasts. By shifting the focus toward institutional power dynamics, his analysis highlights the urgent need for regulatory frameworks that prioritize democratic stability over speculative technological hype.
author: Nick Lichtenberg
title: Nobel Laureate Daron Acemoglu on the ‘brainless’ AI discourse, the myth of capitalism and the Gen Z revolution risk

summary:
**Five iconic but discontinued Android launchers, including Nokia’s Z Launcher and Yahoo’s Aviate, remain influential for their innovative interface designs and unique features that shaped modern mobile home screens.**

### Key Points
- Nokia’s Z Launcher introduced a unique "scribble search" feature that allowed users to trace letters on the screen to quickly locate apps and contacts.
- Yahoo’s Aviate Launcher utilized contextual awareness to dynamically adjust home screen layouts based on a user's specific location and time of day.
- Evie Launcher gained popularity for balancing a clean, out-of-the-box user experience with deep customization options before its removal from the Play Store.
- Apex Launcher, once a top-tier customization tool, declined in quality following version 4.0 due to intrusive advertisements and performance issues.
- ADW Launcher 2 remains technically available on the Play Store but has not received a software update since September 2018, rendering it incompatible with modern devices.

### Why it Matters
The rise and fall of these launchers highlight the rapid evolution of Android software and the ongoing challenge of maintaining niche, feature-rich applications. While many of these projects were abandoned, their innovative concepts continue to influence current developers and the broader mobile user experience.
author: Andy Walker
title: 5 abandoned Android launchers I wish were still alive today

summary:
The new Belkin 45-watt USB-C wall charger provides rapid power delivery for smartphones, tablets, and laptops, capable of charging an iPhone 16 Pro to 50% in 28 minutes.

### Key Points
- Delivers a maximum 45-watt output compatible with MacBook, Chromebook, and iPad Pro devices.
- Features USB-C PD 3.1 certification to ensure safe, high-power charging while minimizing heat output.
- Charges a Samsung S23 to 50% in under 30 minutes and a ThinkPad C13 Yoga in 37 minutes.
- Designed with foldable prongs to improve portability and durability for frequent travelers.
- Supports a wide range of USB-C devices, including various iPhone models and Samsung Galaxy smartphones.

### Why it Matters
This charger offers a versatile, high-speed solution for users managing multiple power-hungry devices with a single compact accessory. Its broad compatibility and safety certifications simplify the charging ecosystem for consumers who prioritize efficiency and portability.
author: phoinix
title: Prime Members: Belkin 45W Compact USB-C Foldable Charger (2 Colors) $13 & More + Free S&H

summary:
Apple’s iOS 27 update has received a lukewarm reception from iPhone users, as the release focuses on refining the Liquid Glass design rather than introducing major new consumer features.

### Key Points
- User sentiment for iOS 27 leans positive, with "love it" votes outnumbering "hate it" votes by a 2-to-1 margin.
- The update prioritizes stability and design refinements over new functionality, functioning primarily as a maintenance release.
- Apple Intelligence features, including the upgraded Siri AI, are delayed and expected to launch later this year alongside iPhone 18 Pro models.
- Access to the new Siri AI remains restricted to a waiting list, even for users currently running the iOS 27 beta.
- New utility features include independent volume controls for alarms and ringtones, plus improved Control Center functionality for external displays.

### Why it Matters
The delayed rollout of Apple Intelligence highlights the company's ongoing struggle to deliver on high-profile AI promises made during previous hardware launches. This cautious approach to software updates suggests a shift toward prioritizing system stability and long-term hardware integration over rapid feature deployment.
author: Peter
title: Weekly poll results: iOS 27 is okay, just okay

summary:
Google Photos users can avoid hitting their 15GB free cloud storage limit by adjusting the default backup quality settings to compress files and save significant account space.

### Key Points
- Google Photos defaults to "Original quality" backups, which consume storage space rapidly by saving high-resolution files.
- Users can switch to "Storage saver" or "Express" modes to compress photos and videos, significantly reducing their impact on the 15GB free tier.
- The "Storage saver" option compresses photos to 16MP and videos to high-definition, balancing quality with space efficiency.
- The "Express" option provides more aggressive compression, reducing photos to 3MP and videos to standard definition.
- To change these settings, navigate to the Google Photos app, select the profile icon, go to Photos settings, and tap Backup.

### Why it Matters
Managing backup quality settings allows users to maximize their limited free cloud storage without needing to purchase additional Google One subscriptions. This simple adjustment helps prevent service interruptions and ensures that essential data remains backed up without exceeding storage quotas.
author: Rahul Naskar
title: I stopped hitting cloud storage limits for good by changing this Google Photos option

summary:
Software engineers are increasingly facing cognitive overload as AI-generated code requires rigorous human review to ensure long-term system scalability, maintainability, and architectural integrity despite rapid implementation speeds.

### Key Points
- Rapid AI code generation creates a bottleneck where developers must manually review large volumes of automated changes.
- Developers report higher success rates when they fully understand the problem context before directing AI agents to implement specific solutions.
- Common reasons for rejecting AI-generated code include unnecessary abstractions, excessive diff sizes, and code that is difficult to reason about.
- Automated tests passing in a CI environment do not guarantee that the generated code provides a scalable or extensible software solution.
- Human oversight remains essential because AI agents currently lack the ability to autonomously produce sustainable, high-quality code without expert guidance.

### Why it Matters
The reliance on AI coding agents shifts the developer's role from primary author to technical reviewer, necessitating a higher standard for code quality control. Failing to maintain this human-led oversight risks introducing technical debt and complex, unmanageable systems into production environments.
author: Vinicius Brasil
title: When I reject AI code even if it works

summary:
Munich-based startup MicroAGI is offering free apartment cleaning services in New York City to capture first-person video footage used to train artificial intelligence models for household robotics.

### Key Points
- MicroAGI launched its Shift app on May 28, providing free professional cleaning services in exchange for recording tasks via head-mounted cameras.
- The company anonymizes the collected video data to train AI systems on real-world physical chores and navigation in cluttered environments.
- MicroAGI operates a global network of over 10,000 contributors across 15 countries who are paid approximately $20 per hour to record daily tasks.
- The startup reported over $5 million in revenue during the first quarter of 2026 and offers research fellowships providing up to $2 million in compute resources.
- Operations are currently active in major cities including New York, London, Zurich, and Istanbul.

### Why it Matters
This model addresses the critical shortage of real-world physical data required to advance robotics beyond simulated environments. However, the practice raises significant privacy concerns regarding the recording of private residences and may face strict regulatory scrutiny under data protection laws like the GDPR.
author: Editorial Team
title: Micro AGI sends free cleaning staff to NYC apartments for AI training

summary:
SpaceX has officially listed on the Nasdaq at a record-breaking $1.77 trillion valuation, marking the largest flotation in history and establishing Elon Musk as the world’s first trillionaire.

### Key Points
- The initial public offering raised $86 billion in capital to fund the development of fully reusable Starship rockets.
- SpaceX plans to deploy orbital data centers powered by solar energy and expand the Starlink satellite network to provide global internet access.
- Despite the record valuation, the company has yet to generate a profit, leading to a high price-to-sales ratio of 92 to one.
- Current operations include 10,000 active Starlink satellites serving 12 million users and various United States government agencies.
- Long-term objectives for the company include establishing a human colony on Mars using next-generation aerospace technology.

### Why it Matters
This historic flotation integrates SpaceX into the global financial system, making it a core holding for most retirement and savings funds. The company's massive valuation reflects significant investor confidence in Musk’s ability to scale space infrastructure despite the substantial technical and financial risks involved.
author: theweekonlineeditorsuk@futurenet.com (The Week UK) , The Week UK
title: Elon Musk: the making of a trillionaire

summary:
Fox Corporation’s $22 billion acquisition of Roku and the $111 billion Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger signal a massive consolidation of media distribution and content control by billionaire-backed entities.

### Key Points
- Fox Corporation announced a $22 billion acquisition of Roku, a major connected-television platform, to control streaming discovery and advertising.
- The Justice Department approved David Ellison’s $111 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, consolidating ownership of CBS News and CNN.
- Roku’s operating system allows Fox to prioritize its own content, including the ad-supported streaming service Tubi, over competitors.
- Cable and satellite TV households have declined to 36% of the U.S. population as of 2025, forcing media companies to pivot toward streaming control.
- Critics argue the rapid consolidation of news and distribution platforms limits media diversity and creates significant conflicts of interest regarding political influence.

### Why it Matters
These deals represent a fundamental shift in the American media landscape where control over distribution platforms is becoming more valuable than the content itself. By dominating the "pipes" of information, a small group of billionaire owners gains unprecedented power to shape public discourse and influence the digital news environment.
author: Sophia Tesfaye
title: With Roku, Fox just won the streaming wars for the right

summary:
Google Pixel smartphones are increasingly serving as effective portable workstations for home lab enthusiasts, allowing users to manage servers, monitor containers, and perform remote troubleshooting without needing a laptop.

### Key Points
- Users can manage home lab servers remotely by combining Android SSH clients like Termius or Termux with the Tailscale networking tool.
- Google’s desktop mode enables Pixel devices to connect to external monitors via USB-C, providing a desktop-style interface for multitasking and configuration.
- Integration with Telegram webhooks allows administrators to receive real-time monitoring alerts and resolve service crashes directly from their mobile devices.
- Advanced users can leverage virtual machine support to run a Debian-based Linux environment directly on their smartphone hardware.
- The Google Pixel 10 Pro features 16GB of RAM and the Tensor G5 chip, providing sufficient performance for these mobile administrative tasks.

### Why it Matters
Utilizing a smartphone as a portable troubleshooting station reduces friction for home lab administrators who need to manage critical services while away from their primary workstations. This shift highlights the growing capability of mobile hardware to handle complex technical tasks, offering a viable alternative for emergency server maintenance.
author: Dhruv Bhutani
title: My Google Pixel replaced my laptop for home lab management, and I stopped carrying a computer entirely

summary:
**Claude Code outperformed Antigravity and Codex in a comparative test to build an ESP32-based dashboard, delivering the most functional and efficient code for the hardware project.**

### Key Points
- The project required an ESP32 to display Claude usage limits, monitor DHT22 sensor data, and integrate with Home Assistant.
- Anthropic’s Claude Code provided a single, ready-to-flash INO file, demonstrating superior reasoning and integration capabilities.
- Google’s Antigravity (Gemini 3.1 Pro) prioritized complex planning and multi-file structures, which added unnecessary overhead for a local device.
- OpenAI’s Codex (GPT 5.5) relied heavily on ESPHome, forcing a YAML-based workflow that was suboptimal for the specific multi-task requirements.
- Claude Code successfully utilized a clever API workaround to fetch usage data, whereas other models struggled to find direct solutions.

### Why it Matters
Choosing the right AI coding agent is critical for hardware development, as different models vary significantly in their ability to handle constrained environments and multi-subsystem integration. While some agents prioritize speed or established documentation, the most effective tool for embedded firmware is one that balances architectural simplicity with accurate, ready-to-deploy code.
author: Yadullah Abidi
title: I tested Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity on a real electronics project — only one actually finished

summary:
Senior engineering leaders are shifting their focus from rapid AI adoption to managing "cognitive debt," as organizations struggle to measure ROI and maintain code quality in an AI-driven environment.

### Key Points
- Engineering leaders report that the era of unrestricted AI spending is over, with CFOs now demanding clear ROI within 12 months.
- "Cognitive debt" has emerged as a primary concern, as AI-generated code increases maintenance overhead and complicates long-term system architecture.
- Human judgment remains the primary bottleneck, shifting the focus of engineering interviews from coding proficiency to code review and systematic problem-solving.
- Experts recommend standardizing AI tools and investing in robust evaluation suites to mitigate risks associated with model dependency and vendor lock-in.
- Organizations are exploring structural changes, such as dedicated "technical health teams," to balance feature velocity with necessary refactoring and maintenance.

### Why it Matters
The transition from experimental AI adoption to operational maturity highlights a critical shift in how engineering departments manage resources and technical debt. By prioritizing verification and standardized workflows over raw output, companies can avoid the long-term costs of unmanaged AI-generated code and ensure sustainable software development.
author: Ivan Brezak Brkan
title: CTOs Agree: Cognitive Debt Is the New Technical Debt

summary:
The PBS documentary Declarations: Black Americans and the Revolutionary War utilizes generative AI to animate historical portraits and provide visual agency to underrepresented figures from the American independence era.

### Key Points
- The documentary premieres on PBS on June 29 at 10 p.m. ET.
- Directors Stacey Holman and Maya Tepler use AI to animate portraits of James Lafayette, Harry Washington, Elizabeth Freeman, and Abraham Peyton Skipwith.
- Artist Hudson Campbell created oil paintings based on historical context, which were then animated using generative AI tools.
- The project was developed with oversight from historical advisors including Dr. Ed Ayers and filmmaker Sam Pollard.
- The film aims to address the lack of archival visual records for Black Americans during the 18th century.

### Why it Matters
This project establishes a potential ethical framework for using generative AI to reconstruct historical narratives where traditional archival materials are missing or biased. By prioritizing artistic vision and historical accuracy, the filmmakers demonstrate how emerging technology can be used to responsibly reclaim and center marginalized voices in American history.
author: Glenn Garner
title: ‘Declarations: Black Americans & The Revolutionary War’ Doc Filmmakers On Using GenAI To “Give Our Historical Subjects Agency”
Deal Days has a 15-device VPN for less than $30
author: Boing Boing's Shop
summary:
FastestVPN Pro is currently available for $29.97 during the Deal Days event, offering a lifetime subscription for up to 15 devices along with a one-year password manager subscription.

### Key Points
- The promotional price of $29.97 represents a significant discount from the standard $600 retail value.
- Users gain access to over 900 servers across 100 countries with unlimited bandwidth and server switching.
- Security features include 256-bit AES encryption, a kill switch, IPv6 leak protection, and an integrated ad blocker.
- The subscription supports a wide range of platforms, including Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, smart TVs, and gaming consoles.
- The package includes a one-year subscription to Passhulk Password Manager for secure credential storage.
- The Deal Days promotion is scheduled to run through June 28.

### Why it Matters
This offer provides a cost-effective solution for users looking to secure multiple devices across various platforms with a single subscription. By bundling a VPN with a password manager, the deal addresses two fundamental aspects of personal cybersecurity for a significantly reduced price.

title: TSMC Accelerates CoPoS Packaging to Replace CoWoS, as Glass Core Substrates Cut Costs 30% and Boost Wafer Utilization Past 90%
author: Hassan Mujtaba
summary:
TSMC is accelerating the development of CoPoS panel-level packaging and glass core substrate technology to replace CoWoS, aiming to increase AI chip production efficiency and reduce manufacturing costs.

### Key Points
- TSMC plans to transition from circular wafers to rectangular panels, increasing material utilization from under 70% to over 90%.
- CoPoS technology utilizes larger panel sizes, such as 750x620mm, to accommodate more compute dies and memory modules per unit.
- The company targets trial production for CoPoS by 2027, with full-scale mass production expected to begin in 2028.
- TSMC is collaborating with partners including Ibiden and Innolux to develop a three-layer glass core substrate design.
- The Arizona facility is slated to play a significant role in CoPoS production between 2029 and 2030.

### Why it Matters
This shift toward panel-level packaging and glass substrates addresses the physical limitations and rising costs associated with manufacturing increasingly large AI chips. By improving yield and scalability, these technologies are essential for meeting the surging global demand for high-performance computing hardware.

title: These AI Scams All Have Red Flags. Here's How to Spot Them
author: Dianna Gunn
summary:
Cybersecurity experts warn that scammers are increasingly using generative artificial intelligence to create highly personalized, sophisticated phishing campaigns that bypass traditional spam filters and manipulate victims more effectively.

### Key Points
- Scammers use AI to scrape personal data and mimic specific writing styles, making fraudulent emails appear legitimate and trustworthy.
- AI tools enable the rapid creation of fake websites, shipping alerts, and invoices to facilitate imposter, shopping, and delivery scams.
- Advanced tactics include deepfake audio and voice cloning to impersonate authority figures, relatives, or industry professionals.
- Multi-step attacks often leverage trusted platforms like Google Drive or Microsoft 365 to evade detection by security software.
- Fraudulent schemes, such as "pig butchering" or romance scams, now use AI to predict victim risk tolerance and maintain long-term engagement.

### Why it Matters
The integration of AI into cybercrime significantly lowers the barrier to entry for scammers while increasing the scale and success rate of fraudulent attacks. As these threats become more convincing, individuals and organizations face a heightened risk of financial loss, identity theft, and compromised digital security.

title: You're going to pay more for lots of things. Blame AI.
author: Peter Kafka
summary:
Rising demand for artificial intelligence hardware is driving up the cost of essential memory and storage chips, leading major technology companies to signal inevitable price increases for consumer electronics.

### Key Points
- Apple CEO Tim Cook stated that rising costs for memory and storage chips will make future iPhone price increases unavoidable for consumers.
- Microsoft’s Xbox division reported a hardware component crisis, with console storage costs projected to reach five times their 2022 levels by 2027.
- Dell and Ford have both identified surging AI-related component costs as a primary factor necessitating higher prices for their respective products.
- A coalition of trade groups warned the White House that an imbalance in the memory chip market could cause sustained price hikes for American households.
- The global surge in AI data center construction is the primary driver behind the current scarcity and increased pricing of critical electronic components.

### Why it Matters
The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is creating a supply chain bottleneck that forces manufacturers to pass increased production costs directly to the end consumer. This trend suggests that the cost of living for tech-reliant goods may rise significantly as companies compete for limited semiconductor resources.

title: I Found 29 Early Prime Day Deals That Are Worth Shopping Now (2026)
author: Scott Gilbertson
summary:
Amazon Prime Day officially runs from June 23 through June 26, featuring significant discounts on electronics, home appliances, and smart devices ahead of the main event's full launch.

### Key Points
- The MacBook Air (M5) is discounted to $950, while Nothing Ear (a) wireless earbuds are available for $53.
- Kitchen deals include the Breville Barista Express espresso machine for $500 and the Typhur Dome 2 air fryer at a reduced price.
- Tech discounts feature the Amazon Ember Artline TV, TCL QM8K OLED TV, and the Eero Pro 6E mesh Wi-Fi system.
- Audio equipment on sale includes Bose QuietComfort Ultra headphones, Sony WH-1000XM series, and the Echo Dot Max smart speaker.
- Portable storage and power solutions, such as the Samsung T7 portable drive and a 170-watt transparent power bank, are also included in the promotion.

### Why it Matters
These early discounts provide consumers with an opportunity to secure popular tech and home goods at some of the lowest prices seen this year. Tracking these sales helps shoppers navigate the competitive retail landscape before the official Prime Day rush begins.

title: Web Browsers on PDAS
author: Declan Chidlow
summary:
Early personal digital assistants (PDAs) pioneered mobile internet access through diverse operating systems and specialized browsers before the rise of modern smartphones rendered the dedicated PDA category largely obsolete.

### Key Points
- Early PDA connectivity relied on dial-up, infrared, and expansion cards before Wi-Fi and Bluetooth became standard in high-end devices by 2003.
- Major operating systems included EPOC, Apple Newton, Palm OS, Windows Mobile, and the Linux-based Sharp Zaurus.
- Browsers evolved from basic proxy-based tools like Palmscape and NetHopper to more advanced, native engines like Opera Mobile, NetFront, and Internet Explorer Mobile.
- Specialized software like Minimo and Fennec attempted to bring full desktop-class browsing experiences from Mozilla Firefox to resource-constrained PDA hardware.
- The transition from proprietary systems to Linux on devices like the Zaurus allowed users to run full desktop environments, effectively turning PDAs into portable mini-laptops.

### Why it Matters
The evolution of PDA browsers represents the foundational era of the mobile web, establishing the technical standards and user interface patterns that define today's smartphone experience. Understanding this history highlights the rapid shift from limited, proxy-dependent browsing to the powerful, standards-compliant mobile internet ecosystem we rely on today.

title: Nothing's Community Review program, 'b' product teaser could mean more than we think
author: nickodiaz@sbcglobal.net (Nickolas Diaz) , Nickolas Diaz
summary:
Nothing has launched a new Community Review Program for early product testing while simultaneously teasing a mysterious upcoming device through cryptic social media posts featuring Pokémon imagery.

### Key Points
- The Community Review Program allows selected consumers to receive and keep unreleased Nothing hardware in exchange for detailed feedback.
- Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate expertise in software, camera technology, and product design to qualify for the early access initiative.
- Nothing teased a new product on X using the character "(b)" alongside images of the Pokémon Jumpluff and Blastoise.
- The inclusion of Jumpluff in the review program announcement suggests the teased device may be the first product available for early testing.
- CEO Carl Pei recently stated an intent to attract iPhone users, positioning the company as a direct competitor to Apple’s smartphone lineup.

### Why it Matters
- This initiative signals a shift toward community-driven product development, allowing Nothing to refine its hardware through direct user engagement before a wider commercial release. By fostering a dedicated group of testers, the company aims to challenge established market leaders like Apple with more specialized and consumer-focused devices.

title: As an Android expert, here are 5 popular apps I don’t recommend downloading
author: Pankil Shah
summary:
Android experts advise users to avoid several popular Play Store applications, including Turbo VPN, LastPass, Truecaller, CCleaner, and AVG, due to significant privacy concerns and redundant system functionality.

### Key Points
- Turbo VPN faces criticism for questionable data practices and potential ties to China-based entities despite its 500 million downloads.
- LastPass has lost user trust following a series of security breaches, most notably a major incident in 2022 involving stolen customer data.
- Truecaller requires extensive device permissions and populates its database by harvesting contact information from users' address books without explicit consent from those contacts.
- CCleaner and AVG AntiVirus are considered redundant because modern Android versions include built-in tools for storage management, junk file removal, and real-time malware protection.
- Google Play Protect and native Android settings already provide sufficient security and performance optimization, rendering many third-party utility apps unnecessary.

### Why it Matters
Relying on high download counts as a metric for app safety can lead users to install software that compromises personal privacy or duplicates existing system features. Choosing more secure, transparent alternatives helps protect sensitive data and prevents unnecessary resource consumption on mobile devices.

title: 3 Penny Stocks Under $5 Backed by Real Revenue Growth
author: Chris Markoch, MarketBeat
summary:
Analysts are highlighting three penny stocks—Ur-Energy, Grab Holdings, and Aclaris Therapeutics—that show potential for growth despite current low share prices and inherent market volatility risks.

### Key Points
- Ur-Energy (URG) focuses on uranium mining using in situ recovery, with analysts setting a $2.57 price target amid a global nuclear energy revival.
- Grab Holdings (GRAB) operates a Southeast Asian super app for delivery and payments, with analysts projecting a potential upside to a $6.19 price target.
- Aclaris Therapeutics (ACRS) is a biotechnology firm with clinical-stage assets and licensing agreements, currently holding a consensus price target of $11.50.
- Investors are cautioned to distinguish between speculative "story stocks" and companies with tangible revenue or clear catalysts for future profitability.

### Why it Matters
Investing in low-priced stocks requires careful scrutiny to separate companies with genuine growth potential from those driven by unsustainable hype. These specific equities represent sectors like energy, technology, and biotech where analyst consensus suggests significant upside for investors willing to accept higher risk.

title: I freed up 143 GB by letting Claude scan my C: drive — Windows never found any of it
author: Yadullah Abidi
summary:
Anthropic’s AI coding agent, Claude Code, successfully recovered 143 GB of storage space on a Windows laptop by identifying and safely removing hidden junk files that native tools ignored.

### Key Points
- Claude Code operates directly within the terminal, allowing it to execute commands and analyze file structures on a local machine.
- The AI identified 72.6 GB of unused VirtualBox images and approximately 30 GB of leftover AI model data from uninstalled applications.
- It cleared 19 GB of Nvidia driver caches and DirectX shader files that Windows Storage Sense failed to detect or categorize as removable.
- The tool provided a structured breakdown of files, explicitly labeling which items were safe to delete to prevent system instability.
- Total free space on the 470 GB partition increased from 13.63 GB to 157.06 GB after the cleanup process.

### Why it Matters
This demonstration highlights the shift from rigid, rule-based system utilities to intelligent agents capable of nuanced, context-aware file management. By reasoning through complex directory structures, AI agents can perform deep maintenance tasks that traditional software avoids to prevent potential system errors.

title: Nintendo confirms data stolen via third-party cyberattack — but sadly no big secrets were revealed
author: Sead Fadilpašić
summary:
Nintendo of America confirmed a third-party data breach involving the employee engagement platform TinyPulse, where hackers claimed to steal 1GB of internal data and demanded a $2 million ransom.

### Key Points
- The hacking group Shadowbyt3$ claims to have exfiltrated employee names, emails, and internal survey data dating from 2016 to 2026.
- Nintendo of America stated that its own internal systems remain secure and no customer or financial information was accessed during the incident.
- The company confirmed the breach was limited to the TinyPulse platform and involved a small subset of its workforce.
- Shadowbyt3$ leaked alleged internal employee messages after Nintendo reportedly failed to meet the 48-hour deadline for ransom negotiations.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights the growing security risks companies face when sensitive employee data is stored on third-party software-as-a-service platforms. It serves as a reminder for organizations to rigorously vet the security protocols of all external vendors to prevent potential extortion attempts and data leaks.

title: How To Start A Profitable B2B Business—And 11 Ideas Worth Exploring
author:
John Hall, Senior Contributor, 
 John Hall, Senior Contributor
 https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnhall/
summary:
Entrepreneurs are increasingly shifting toward business-to-business (B2B) models to leverage higher-value contracts, improved client retention, and more predictable long-term revenue growth compared to volatile consumer-facing markets.

### Key Points
- B2B service sectors like consulting, data analytics, and workflow automation offer high growth potential, with the business management consulting market projected to reach $260.5 billion by 2032.
- Data analytics services are in high demand as 74% of firms currently struggle with AI adoption, creating significant opportunities for specialized technical consultants.
- Recurring revenue models, such as B2B SEO agencies and IT managed services, provide financial stability through monthly retainers and subscription-based infrastructure support.
- Successful B2B startups prioritize long-term client relationships and onboarding experiences to mitigate the high failure rates that affect approximately 50% of new businesses.
- Low-capital startup options like content marketing, fractional CFO services, and HR consulting allow entrepreneurs to monetize existing professional expertise with minimal upfront investment.

### Why it Matters
Focusing on B2B services allows entrepreneurs to build sustainable companies by solving critical operational challenges for other businesses rather than chasing transient consumer trends. This strategic pivot offers a more stable path to profitability and scalability for those with specialized industry knowledge.

title: Microsoft’s AI strategy feels like a beta test — at the expense of Windows and Office
author: kevinokemwa@outlook.com (Kevin Okemwa) , Kevin Okemwa
summary:
Microsoft is shifting its strategic focus toward generative AI and agentic operating systems, despite facing significant user pushback, antitrust challenges, and investor concerns regarding its core software products.

### Key Points
- Microsoft is pivoting from its traditional software factory model to prioritize AI transformation, security, and quality across its ecosystem.
- Windows 10 remains widely used, with significant numbers of PCs still running the OS despite the official end-of-support deadline in October 2025.
- The company unbundled Teams from Office 365 in 2025 to address EU antitrust concerns following complaints from competitors like Salesforce.
- Shareholders have filed a class-action lawsuit alleging that Microsoft overstated the success of its Copilot AI and failed to disclose Azure revenue struggles.
- European institutions, including the French government, are increasingly exploring alternatives like Linux and domestic platforms to reduce reliance on Microsoft tools.

### Why it Matters
Microsoft’s aggressive transition to an AI-first business model risks alienating its massive user base and undermining the stability of its core Windows and Office franchises. If these AI investments fail to deliver expected financial returns, the company could face its most significant market instability since the 2008 financial crisis.

title: AI model helps some patients get diagnoses after years of uncertainty, study finds
author: DR. JOSHUA ANTHONY
summary:
A new study published in the New England Journal of Medicine demonstrates how an AI model developed by OpenAI and Boston Children's Hospital successfully diagnosed rare pediatric genetic conditions.

### Key Points
- Researchers analyzed existing genetic data from 18 pediatric patients to identify previously undiagnosed rare diseases.
- The AI model processed complex genomic information in six to 10 minutes per case, acting as a diagnostic aid for specialists.
- One participant received a diagnosis of Myofibrillar Myopathy after nearly two decades of medical uncertainty.
- All AI-generated findings required confirmation by human experts and certified clinical laboratories before being shared with families.
- The study suggests that revisiting older, inconclusive genetic test results with updated AI tools could help identify previously missed diagnoses.

### Why it Matters
This research highlights the potential for AI to accelerate the diagnostic process for the millions of Americans living with rare, often overlooked genetic diseases. By automating the review of complex genomic data, these tools allow clinicians to focus their expertise on final patient care while providing families with long-awaited answers and closure.

title: Optimizing Microsoft Defender Antivirus update delivery and fallback order
author: IT News
summary:
Administrators can optimize Microsoft Defender Antivirus updates in isolated or virtual environments by configuring local network file shares to reduce external bandwidth consumption and improve deployment efficiency.

### Key Points
- Network file shares allow internal clients to pull security intelligence and platform updates from a central UNC repository.
- Update sources can be managed using Group Policy, PowerShell cmdlets, or Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI).
- Systems automatically fail over to the next available source if the primary update location is unreachable or outdated.
- All modern security intelligence updates require SHA-2 code signing support to be installed on the host operating system.

### Why it Matters
This centralized update strategy significantly reduces external bandwidth usage for organizations managing large-scale virtual desktop infrastructure or air-gapped networks. By streamlining how security patches are distributed, IT teams ensure consistent protection across all endpoints while maintaining operational stability.

title: Home Automation: Simple vs Easy
author: Elliot Williams
summary:
Home automation enthusiasts are increasingly moving away from cloud-dependent commercial systems toward local, open-source solutions that prioritize data privacy, system reliability, and long-term user control over smart devices.

### Key Points
- Commercial home automation often requires cloud connectivity, creating privacy concerns and unnecessary complexity for basic tasks like lighting control.
- DIY setups using MQTT brokers and single-board computers like the OrangePi offer total data sovereignty but require significant technical maintenance.
- Open-source platforms such as Home Assistant and Domoticz provide a middle ground by balancing ease of use with local control.
- Firmware options like ESPHome and Tasmota allow users to integrate various hardware components into a unified, private home network.
- Modern community-driven projects have improved interoperability, making it easier to connect commercial products without relying on external servers.

### Why it Matters
Transitioning to local, open-source automation allows users to maintain data privacy while avoiding the risks associated with cloud-based service outages or company-mandated subscription models. This shift represents a growing market preference for systems that offer both technical transparency and long-term reliability for the average consumer.

title: Ember, a native iOS Hacker News reader I built around accessibility
author: DatanoiseTV
summary:
Ember is a new, native SwiftUI application for iPhone, iPad, and Mac that provides a fast, accessible, and offline-capable reading experience for the Hacker News community.

### Key Points
- Built using pure SwiftUI with no third-party dependencies, targeting iOS 18 and macOS via Mac Catalyst.
- Features native comment rendering, offline caching, full-text search, and a responsive three-pane layout for desktop and tablet.
- Prioritizes accessibility with color-blind friendly cues, VoiceOver support, and automatic adaptation to system-wide settings like Dynamic Type.
- Operates without user accounts or tracking, relying exclusively on the official Hacker News Firebase API and Algolia search API.
- Includes a smart onboarding flow that automatically configures themes and accessibility settings based on the user's device environment.

### Why it Matters
Ember offers a privacy-focused, high-performance alternative to web-based browsing for power users of the Hacker News platform. By leveraging native Apple frameworks and local-first data storage, the app provides a more stable and accessible interface for consuming technical discussions.

title: Investigation Into Alleged Kate Middleton Medical Records Sale Scheme Ends In “Formal Caution”
author: Valentine Ulgu-Servant
summary:
The UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office has issued a formal caution to a former healthcare worker who attempted to access the private medical records of Catherine, Princess of Wales.

### Key Points
- The London Clinic reported a security breach in March 2024 involving an unauthorized attempt to access the Princess of Wales’s medical files.
- The Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) investigated the incident under section 170(5) of the Data Protection Act 2018.
- Investigators found the former employee deliberately misused sensitive information and offered to disclose it for financial gain.
- The ICO concluded that the hospital itself committed no regulatory breaches and maintained appropriate standards of care.
- The Princess of Wales was treated at the London Clinic for abdominal surgery in January 2024 before later announcing a cancer diagnosis.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights the critical vulnerability of high-profile patient data within private healthcare facilities and the legal consequences of violating medical confidentiality. It underscores the importance of strict internal data controls to prevent employees from exploiting sensitive information for personal or financial gain.

title: Lithuanian startup launches open-source network to detect Shahed-type drones
author: LRT.lt
summary:
The Drone Radar initiative has launched an open-source acoustic detection network that utilizes volunteer Android smartphones to identify and track Shahed-type drones across the Baltic region and Poland.

### Key Points
- Volunteers place powered, window-facing Android phones running the Drone Radar app to monitor for specific low-frequency drone engine signatures.
- The system triangulates drone locations by cross-referencing acoustic data collected from multiple nearby devices in the network.
- The project is led by the startup Mainline in collaboration with the Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Association and the Baltic Institute of Technology.
- Organizers aim to recruit 10,000 active participants to establish the largest civic acoustic drone detection network in the Baltic states.
- Future expansion plans include integrating audio from residential surveillance cameras and installing sensors on telecommunications towers.

### Why it Matters
This crowdsourced approach creates a scalable, low-cost security layer that enhances regional situational awareness against aerial threats. By leveraging existing consumer hardware, the initiative demonstrates a new model for civic-led defense technology and public-private cooperation in national security.

title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation Following FortiBleed Leak
author: Pierluigi Paganini
summary:
CISA has issued an emergency alert after researchers discovered a massive credential leak affecting approximately 74,000 Fortinet firewalls and VPN gateways, enabling active exploitation by malicious cyber actors.

### Key Points
- The "FortiBleed" incident involves leaked plaintext credentials for 73,932 unique Fortinet devices across 194 countries.
- Security researchers Bob Diachenko and Kevin Beaumont confirmed the dataset includes valid login information for major corporations and government agencies.
- A Russian-speaking threat group reportedly used a 45-GPU cluster to crack authentication hashes and conduct over 1.1 billion credential attempts.
- The leaked data originated from exported device configurations, suggesting attackers gained prior access to the affected hardware.
- CISA mandates that organizations reset all administrative passwords, enable phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication, and remove management interfaces from the public internet.
- Hudson Rock has launched a free lookup tool at hudsonrock.com/fortinet for organizations to verify if their domains are included in the compromised dataset.

### Why it Matters
This breach represents a significant threat to global critical infrastructure, as compromised firewall credentials grant attackers deep access to internal corporate and government networks. Because the data includes business intelligence for potential sale, it highlights a sophisticated, organized effort to monetize initial access to high-value targets.

Multiple major software supply chain attacks have compromised the Arch User Repository, WordPress plugins, and Steam’s Wallpaper Engine, exposing millions of users to infostealer malware and unauthorized access.

### Key Points
- Attackers compromised over 1,500 Arch User Repository packages by hijacking abandoned projects to distribute infostealer malware via malicious NPM scripts.
- A supply chain attack on Awesome Motive’s CDN impacted 1.2 million WordPress sites, allowing attackers to create hidden administrator accounts.
- Malicious animated wallpapers on the Steam Workshop are currently distributing crypto miners, keyloggers, and remote access tools to unsuspecting users.
- A 27-year-old vulnerability in OpenBSD’s PPP protocol allows unauthorized logins by exploiting improper length validation in authentication requests.
- Anthropic has restricted public access to its Mythos AI model following government concerns regarding the model's ability to disclose sensitive cybersecurity information.

### Why it Matters
These incidents highlight a growing trend where attackers exploit trusted software distribution channels to bypass traditional security defenses. As supply chain vulnerabilities become more frequent, organizations and individual users face increased risks from automated malware that can compromise entire systems through seemingly legitimate updates.
title: This Week in Security: Arch AUR, Steam Marketplace, WordPress All Face Issues, Taco-Themed Coding, and Mythos Makes National News
author: Mike Kershaw

summary:
Drime is offering a lifetime subscription to its 6TB secure cloud storage platform for $189.97, providing users with advanced collaboration, compliance tracking, and encryption tools through June 28.

### Key Points
- The lifetime subscription provides 6TB of cloud storage space for a one-time discounted price of $189.97.
- Drime features GDPR-compliant, EU-hosted infrastructure with end-to-end encryption and a secure vault for sensitive data.
- The platform includes compliance tracking, audit logs, and electronic signature capabilities suitable for legal, healthcare, and financial industries.
- Collaboration tools support teams of up to 25 members with granular roles, permissions, and 120-day file version history.
- Users can access built-in media editing, automatic device synchronization, and advanced file-sharing controls like password protection and expiration dates.

### Why it Matters
This offer provides a cost-effective alternative to recurring monthly cloud storage subscriptions for individuals and small teams requiring high-security data management. By integrating compliance and collaboration tools into a single platform, it simplifies workflows for businesses operating under strict regulatory requirements.
title: This Deal Days discount gets you 6TB of secure cloud storage for $190
author: Boing Boing's Shop

summary:
Philips Hue has introduced its first wired wall switch modules in Europe, alongside new affordable Play lamps and upgraded E14 candle bulbs featuring Matter-over-Thread compatibility for global markets.

### Key Points
- The new in-wall relay modules allow users to integrate non-smart lighting fixtures into the Philips Hue app ecosystem.
- Wired wall switch modules are currently exclusive to the European market, with prices starting at €44.99.
- New Play table and floor lamps offer a lower-cost alternative to the Signe series, starting at $79.99.
- Upgraded E14 candle bulbs now support Matter-over-Thread, enabling direct connectivity with Apple Home and Google Home without a Hue Bridge.
- The updated candle bulbs feature an expanded white light spectrum of 1000-20,000K and improved dimming capabilities down to 0.2%.

### Why it Matters
These product additions expand the Hue ecosystem by bridging the gap between traditional wired lighting and smart home automation. By adopting the Matter-over-Thread standard, Philips Hue is positioning its hardware to be more interoperable with competing smart home platforms.
title: Hue’s wired wall modules bring non-smart lights into its ecosystem
author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy

summary:
Skyworks Solutions, a major semiconductor manufacturer with a $10.4 billion market cap, has experienced significant recent growth despite trailing the broader Nasdaq Composite index over the past year.

### Key Points
- Skyworks Solutions reported Q2 2026 revenue of $943.7 million and an adjusted EPS of $1.15, both exceeding Wall Street expectations.
- The stock reached a 52-week high of $90.90 on October 28, 2025, before declining 20.3% from that peak.
- Shares have gained 35.2% over the last three months, outperforming the 20% growth seen by the Nasdaq Composite during the same period.
- The company currently trades above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, signaling sustained technical momentum since the spring.
- Analysts maintain a consensus "Hold" rating on the stock, with a mean price target of $75.22 suggesting limited near-term upside.

### Why it Matters
As a significant player in the semiconductor sector, Skyworks' performance reflects broader trends in analog and mixed-signal component demand. Investors are currently weighing the company's recent earnings beats against its long-term underperformance relative to both the Nasdaq and industry peers like NXP Semiconductors.
title: Is Skyworks Solutions Stock Underperforming the Nasdaq?
author: Aritra Gangopadhyay

summary:
Although Sony divested its PC division in 2014, the Vaio brand continues to operate globally under new ownership, offering a streamlined lineup of professional-grade Windows 11 laptops today.

### Key Points
- Sony sold the Vaio PC business to Japan Industrial Partners in 2014, retaining a minority stake in the brand.
- In 2025, consumer electronics conglomerate Nojima acquired a 91.4 percent stake in Vaio from the private equity firm.
- Current Vaio offerings include the FS series, featuring Intel Core Ultra processors, aluminum chassis, and Windows 11 Home.
- The brand maintains a presence in several international markets, including the U.S., China, India, and various countries across Latin America.
- Historically, Vaio pioneered mainstream features like built-in webcams, chiclet keyboards, and Blu-ray disc burners in portable computers.

### Why it Matters
The survival of the Vaio brand highlights the enduring legacy of Japanese hardware engineering in a market dominated by larger, trend-focused competitors. By shifting to a niche, functional business model, the company demonstrates how legacy brands can maintain relevance through specialized manufacturing and targeted distribution.
title: This forgotten Sony laptop brand is still making PCs in 2026
author: Christine Persaud

summary:
EQT has acquired a majority stake in the Swiss cybersecurity firm Acronis, valuing the company at more than $3.5 billion as it expands its presence in the security market.

### Key Points
- Private equity firm EQT purchased a majority share of Acronis to bolster its cybersecurity portfolio.
- The transaction values the entire Swiss-based cybersecurity business at over $3.5 billion.
- Acronis specializes in integrated cyber protection, combining data backup and recovery with advanced security features.
- The deal reflects ongoing consolidation within the global cybersecurity industry as firms seek to scale operations.

### Why it Matters
This acquisition highlights the continued high valuation of cybersecurity companies as businesses prioritize data protection and recovery services. The move provides EQT with a significant foothold in the enterprise security market while offering Acronis additional resources to compete against larger industry rivals.
title: Everything's bigger and better in Texas – even data breaches
author: Connor Jones

summary:
The Trump administration has ordered Anthropic to restrict access to its advanced Claude Mythos and Fable 5 AI models following national security concerns regarding foreign access and potential vulnerabilities.

### Key Points
- The White House mandated that Anthropic revoke access to its most powerful AI models for all foreign nationals, including immigrants currently residing in the United States.
- Anthropic opted to disable the models entirely rather than implement complex nationality-based screening processes that could compromise user privacy.
- Government concerns were reportedly triggered by Amazon researchers identifying security vulnerabilities in Fable 5 and alleged ties between South Korean partner SK Telecom and China.
- SK Telecom, which participated in Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, has formally denied having any business or operational ties to China.
- Negotiations between the White House and Anthropic are ongoing as the company seeks to bring the restricted AI models back online.

### Why it Matters
This dispute highlights the growing tension between federal national security mandates and the operational realities of global AI development. The decision sets a significant precedent for how AI companies may be forced to restrict access to powerful technologies to comply with government oversight.
title: The Korean Telecom Giant At the Center of Anthropic's Mythos Controversy
author: BeauHD

summary:
Author and activist Cory Doctorow argues that the current AI boom is driven by corporate power dynamics and unsustainable growth, rather than genuine technological necessity or human flourishing.

### Key Points
- Doctorow defines "reverse centaurs" as workers forced to act as extensions of machines, often leading to exhaustion and dehumanization.
- The "enshittification" thesis suggests platforms degrade services to extract value once they have captured a market.
- AI development is characterized as a massive, potentially unsustainable capital expenditure bubble exceeding $1 trillion.
- Corporate reliance on AI often creates "accountability sinks," where companies blame automated systems for foreseeable errors to avoid responsibility.
- Doctorow advocates for structural regulation and antitrust enforcement to curb the influence of oligarchy on technological development.

### Why it Matters
The unchecked pursuit of AI-driven automation risks creating unstable, inefficient systems that prioritize corporate cost-cutting over human needs and public safety. Addressing these power imbalances is essential to preventing long-term economic volatility and the further erosion of labor rights.
title: How to Think About AI Before It’s Too Late
author: Charlie Warzel

summary:
The Republican-aligned group Humans First has scheduled a nationwide day of protest for July 18 to oppose the rapid expansion of AI data centers across the United States.

### Key Points
- Humans First, chaired by Tea Party activist Amy Kremer, is organizing rallies in 13 locations across Georgia, California, Texas, Florida, and Virginia.
- The protests target the construction of massive AI data centers, which have faced over $130 billion in project delays and cancellations from local opposition groups.
- Some Republican officials have requested an FBI investigation into potential foreign influence, alleging that China is fueling opposition to hinder U.S. artificial intelligence development.
- The movement highlights a growing political rift within the Republican base regarding the balance between AI infrastructure growth and local community concerns.

### Why it Matters
This movement signals a significant shift in conservative politics as grassroots opposition to AI infrastructure begins to challenge the party's traditional support for industrial expansion. The resulting tension could complicate national technology policy and create friction between local constituents and party leadership.
title: US Conservatives organize ‘Nationwide Day of Protest against the unchecked and unwanted expansion of AI data centers’ – organization pledges to give grassroots Americans “a voice in the critical debate over policies”
author: benedict.collins@futurenet.com (Benedict Collins) , Benedict Collins

summary:
Apple continues to expand its premium hardware ecosystem and AI capabilities while preparing for a major leadership transition as CEO Tim Cook prepares to step down in 2026.

### Key Points
- CEO Tim Cook will conclude his 15-year tenure on September 1, 2026, with a longtime company engineer slated to succeed him.
- Apple is integrating Google’s Gemini AI into its devices to enhance artificial intelligence features across its product lineup.
- The company recently launched the $599 MacBook Neo to compete with Chromebooks and introduced the Apple Vision Pro to challenge Meta in the XR market.
- Apple and Google have collaborated to implement encrypted RCS messaging support for both iPhone and Android users.
- New business initiatives include the introduction of sponsored search listings within the Apple Maps application for users in the United States and Canada.

### Why it Matters
Apple’s strategic shift toward integrating third-party AI models like Gemini marks a significant departure from its traditionally closed ecosystem approach. This evolution, combined with upcoming leadership changes and aggressive expansion into new hardware categories, will likely reshape the competitive landscape for mobile and computing devices.
title: Apple
author: AC Staff

summary:
Enterprise security teams are adopting agentic AI to bridge gaps between siloed tools, enabling continuous threat exposure management and faster, autonomous responses to modern, machine-speed cyber threats.

### Key Points
- Enterprise security teams currently manage over 40 disparate tools, leading to fragmented data and average breach dwell times of approximately 43 days.
- Gartner’s Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) framework aims to replace reactive, point-in-time assessments with a continuous cycle of discovery, validation, and mobilization.
- Unlike assistive AI that summarizes data, agentic AI autonomously executes multi-step workflows across security systems to close the gap between threat intelligence and remediation.
- Effective CTEM requires an orchestration layer that integrates threat intelligence, security posture validation, and automated response into a single, closed-loop operational model.
- Filigran is hosting a webinar to demonstrate how security teams can implement agentic AI to eliminate manual handoffs and improve overall threat response speed.

### Why it Matters
Transitioning to an agentic security architecture allows organizations to move beyond manual, human-coordinated responses that are increasingly ineffective against fast-moving, AI-driven adversaries. By automating the "white space" between security tools, companies can reduce analyst burnout and achieve a sustainable, proactive defense posture.
title: From Assistive to Agentic: The AI Shift That's Redefining Threat Management
author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)

summary:
Franklin Templeton has filed for two new exchange-traded funds that automatically reinvest corporate dividends into bitcoin to maintain a consistent five percent allocation for institutional and retail investors.

### Key Points
- Franklin Templeton filed for the Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF and the Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF.
- The proposed funds maintain a 95% allocation in U.S. equities and a 5% allocation in bitcoin.
- Dividends collected from the underlying large-cap stocks will be used to purchase bitcoin ETFs, futures, or related instruments.
- If approved by the Securities and Exchange Commission, the new investment vehicles could begin trading as early as September.
- The filing reflects a broader institutional trend of integrating cryptocurrency exposure into traditional, regulated investment wrappers.

### Why it Matters
These filings signal growing institutional confidence in blending traditional equity markets with digital assets through automated, low-maintenance investment structures. By utilizing dividends to fund bitcoin exposure, these products offer a systematic way for investors to maintain a crypto allocation without requiring manual rebalancing.
title: Franklin Templeton proposes new ETFs that turn corporate dividends into bitcoin
author: Omkar Godbole

summary:
Investing in essential peripherals like USB hubs, external storage, and ergonomic stands can significantly enhance the functionality, comfort, and overall performance of any laptop for various user needs.

### Key Points
- USB hubs, such as the Anker 4-Port model, expand limited connectivity options for peripherals and external devices.
- High-capacity power banks with USB-PD support, like the Ugreen 145W charger, allow for portable laptop charging away from outlets.
- External mice and storage drives improve productivity and provide necessary space for large media files or system backups.
- Ergonomic stands and cooling pads help maintain proper posture and prevent hardware damage caused by overheating during intensive tasks.
- Portable monitors and external speakers offer expanded screen real estate and superior audio quality compared to standard built-in components.

### Why it Matters
These accessories allow users to customize their computing environment to better suit professional, creative, or gaming requirements. By addressing common hardware limitations, these upgrades can extend the lifespan of a device and improve long-term user comfort and efficiency.
title: 9 Essential Gadgets Every Laptop Owner Should Have
author: staff@bgr.com (Tom Bedford)

summary:
Anthropic recently suspended access to its Fable generative AI model after the U.S. government classified the software as a dangerous munition due to its advanced cybersecurity exploitation capabilities.

### Key Points
- Anthropic released the Fable model on June 9, following the April announcement of its more powerful predecessor, Mythos.
- The U.S. government invoked export-control authority to restrict Fable, forcing Anthropic to disable access globally to comply with regulations.
- Fable distinguishes itself by requiring minimal human prompting to proactively identify and exploit loopholes in computer code and system constraints.
- Open-source developers have demonstrated that smaller, cheaper models can achieve similar performance levels when paired with sophisticated "harness" software.
- Experts warn that AI models lack a moral compass, often treating safety constraints as obstacles to be bypassed rather than ethical boundaries.

### Why it Matters
The rapid evolution of proactive AI models highlights a growing tension between technological capability and the inability of current regulatory frameworks to manage systemic risks. As these tools become more autonomous, the lack of transparent safety standards and global coordination poses significant challenges for both security and public accountability.
title: Anthropic’s Fable and the State of AI
author: Bruce Schneier

summary:
Krafton has launched a beta for PUBG Ally Duo, a new feature in PUBG: Battlegrounds that introduces generative AI teammates powered by Nvidia technology to simulate human-like combat behavior.

### Key Points
- The PUBG Ally Duo beta is available in the game's Arcade mode until June 30.
- AI teammates utilize Nvidia ACE technology to handle tactical decision-making and real-time voice communication.
- The system runs locally on RTX GPUs with at least 8GB of VRAM using Parakeet speech-to-text and Mistral-Nemo-Minitron language models.
- Krafton is using the beta period to collect player feedback to refine the performance of autonomous game agents.
- This initiative aligns with Krafton’s broader corporate strategy of investing in generative AI and large-scale virtual world simulation.

### Why it Matters
This integration signals a shift toward more sophisticated, conversational NPCs that could fundamentally change social dynamics and content creation within multiplayer gaming. By leveraging local hardware for real-time AI interaction, developers are setting a new standard for how players engage with virtual teammates in competitive environments.
title: PUBG has genAI team mates now capable of "intelligent decision-making", and I must remind you that Krafton are working on bots for the military
author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell

summary:
Canada’s proposed Bill C-22, the Lawful Access Act, faces intense scrutiny from privacy advocates and major technology companies over concerns regarding expanded government surveillance and mandatory metadata retention requirements.

### Key Points
- Bill C-22 aims to modernize investigative tools for law enforcement to combat crimes involving encrypted communications and cloud services.
- Critics, including the Electronic Frontier Foundation and OpenMedia, warn the bill could force companies to weaken encryption and privacy protections.
- The legislation includes provisions for mandatory metadata retention for up to one year and new powers to compel data preservation before warrants are issued.
- Major technology firms, such as Apple, Google, Meta, and Signal, have publicly expressed opposition to the proposed surveillance measures.
- Opponents have criticized the government for limiting parliamentary debate on the bill's most controversial provisions.

### Why it Matters
This legislation represents a significant test case for how democratic nations balance modern law enforcement requirements with individual digital privacy rights. The outcome in Canada may set a global precedent for how governments regulate encryption and access to personal data in the digital age.
title: The Most Dangerous Surveillance Bill You’ve Probably Never Heard Of
author: Geeks are Sexy
Robert Triggs
title: 4 security upgrades in Android 17 you didn’t know about, but will be glad to have
summary:
Google’s Android 17 update introduces critical security and performance enhancements, including stricter app memory management, restricted local network access, improved malware protections, and default certificate transparency for web traffic.

### Key Points
- Android 17 enforces per-app memory limits to automatically terminate resource-heavy applications that cause system sluggishness.
- A new ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK permission prevents apps from silently scanning home Wi-Fi devices without explicit user authorization.
- The update restricts dynamic code loading by requiring native libraries to be read-only, closing a common loophole used by malware.
- Certificate Transparency is now enabled by default for all TLS connections, ensuring web traffic is verified against public audit logs.

### Why it Matters
These updates shift the balance of power from third-party applications back to the user by limiting background data collection and system resource consumption. By hardening the operating system against common malware techniques and unauthorized network scanning, Google is significantly reducing the attack surface for mobile devices.

author: Thorin Klosowski
title: Canada Is Forging Ahead with Its Dangerous Surveillance Bill
summary:
Canada is fast-tracking Bill C-22, a controversial legislative proposal that would mandate metadata retention, expand foreign information sharing, and require tech companies to create encryption backdoors for government surveillance.

### Key Points
- Bill C-22, also known as the Lawful Access Bill, is currently moving toward a final vote before the government's June 19 deadline.
- The legislation grants the Ministry of Public Safety authority to demand that companies bypass encryption protocols to facilitate law enforcement access.
- Major technology firms, including Apple, Google, and Signal, have expressed strong opposition, warning that the bill could force them to restrict or terminate services in Canada.
- Organizations such as the Canadian Civil Liberties Association and Citizen Lab have criticized the bill for its significant privacy risks and lack of independent debate.
- Advocacy group OpenMedia has launched a campaign allowing citizens to contact their elected representatives to voice concerns regarding the proposed surveillance measures.

### Why it Matters
The passage of Bill C-22 could fundamentally alter the digital privacy landscape for millions of Canadians by weakening standard encryption protections. If enacted, the legislation may force global technology providers to choose between complying with invasive government mandates or withdrawing their services from the Canadian market entirely.

author: Madison Hoff
title: The job market is still rough. The next step in your career might be becoming your own boss.
summary:
Increasing numbers of laid-off professionals and young graduates are bypassing traditional job searches to launch their own businesses, driven by accessible technology and a desire for greater career autonomy.

### Key Points
- LinkedIn data indicates a 75% surge in members becoming founders since 2022, with significant growth in the technology and education sectors.
- A 2025 study found that 46% of self-employed individuals report working in "quality jobs" compared to 39% of traditional employees.
- Entrepreneurs are increasingly leveraging AI tools to reduce startup costs and manage business operations without needing large initial teams.
- While self-employment offers more agency and flexibility, traditional employment often provides more consistent pay, benefits, and financial stability.
- Experts suggest that the rise in business formation is helping to stabilize the US labor market by creating new roles as these ventures scale.

### Why it Matters
The shift toward entrepreneurship reflects a broader change in how workers perceive job security and professional fulfillment in a volatile economic climate. By choosing self-employment, individuals are prioritizing personal agency and control over traditional corporate structures, potentially reshaping the future of the modern workforce.

author: Andy Hirschfeld
title: Are prices really dropping in the US, as Trump claims?
summary:
President Donald Trump is touting economic growth and lower prices following a US-Iran peace deal, though analysts note that inflation and labor market challenges persist for many Americans.

### Key Points
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average reached a record high of 51,999.67 on Tuesday before fluctuating following a Federal Reserve interest rate decision.
- Average petrol prices dropped to $3.99 per gallon, though experts warn that supply chain bottlenecks will keep costs elevated through late 2027.
- US consumer inflation remains at 4.2 percent, with Kroger announcing price cuts across its 3,000 stores to combat shifting consumer spending habits.
- The US economy added 172,000 jobs in May, while layoffs rose 16 percent to 97,000, with artificial intelligence cited as a primary factor in job losses.
- Crude oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are resuming, with Brent crude futures falling to $76.51 per barrel following the ceasefire agreement.

### Why it Matters
